Title
Programmable chromatin origami with combinatorial AND-gated bridges to causally control gene expression in epithelial cells and neurons

Summary
Goal: Establish a mark-independent, programmable method to control gene expression by rewiring 3D chromatin architecture with engineered, geometry-defined protein bridges. We build a “local-rule” grammar using orthogonal protein–protein interfaces (PPIs) fused to zinc-finger DNA-binding domains (DBDs) to specify multi-point enhancer–promoter contacts, and require coincident occupancy at multiple genomic addresses (AND-gating) to ensure specificity. We test causal links: engineered 3D change → transcriptional change → cell phenotype, in human epithelial cells and iPSC-derived neurons. This sidesteps endogenous chromatin modifiers and frames regulation as mesoscale mechanics rather than epigenetic editing. Prior looping tools (CLOuD9, LADL, OptoLoop) demonstrate that forced proximity can modulate transcription, but they typically use one bridging chemistry and two-site tethers; multi-contact, rule-based folding with intrinsic combinatorial gating has not been established in living cells. We address that gap. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))

Prior work and gap
- Genome topology emerges from loop extrusion by cohesin and boundary insulation by CTCF, which shapes TADs and modulates enhancer–promoter encounter probabilities. However, the field lacks a general, programmable way to impose synthetic multi-contact topologies at chosen loci with built-in specificity logic. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2151-x?utm_source=openai))
- Forced looping has been achieved by tethering natural loop factors (e.g., LDB1 at β-globin) and by dCas9-based inducible bridges (CLOuD9, LADL/OptoLoop), establishing feasibility of proximity-driven expression control. Yet these systems do not provide a modular “staple” grammar to compose multiple contacts or require multi-site coincidence to stabilize loops. A recent bioorthogonal click approach (BPCL) forms multiway contacts chemically, underscoring the opportunity to realize multi-contact logic with protein interfaces and DNA-protein addressability. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5737898/?utm_source=openai))

Central question (hypothesis and goal merged)
Can a minimal set of orthogonal, geometry-defined protein “staples,” each targeted by compact ZF-DBDs, and assembled only upon coincident multi-site occupancy (AND-gating), re-route enhancer traffic to a selected promoter and produce predictable, reversible changes in burst kinetics and cell phenotype without invoking DNA methylation or histone modifications as the primary mechanism? ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11058250/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Translate DNA-origami-style local rules into chromatin folding by:
- Address layer: ZF-DBDs specify genomic “staple landing pads.”
- Interaction layer: pairs/sets of orthogonal coiled-coil PPIs (e.g., SYNZIP families) encode which addresses bind each other.
- Specificity layer: split, low-affinity subinterfaces that only assemble into a high-avidity bridge when all programmed sites are occupied (logical AND), stabilizing the intended multi-point contact and suppressing off-target loops. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aims

Aim 1. Build and validate an AND-gated, two-to-three point chromatin bridge that increases enhancer–promoter contact dwell time and burst frequency.
- Design: Construct ZF–PPI fusions targeting one promoter-proximal site (P) and two enhancer sites (E1/E2) within a well-characterized reporter safe harbor (e.g., AAVS1) engineered with an MS2-tagged gene. Use orthogonal coiled-coil heterodimers (e.g., SYNZIP1:2, 5:6) split into subinterfaces such that P+E1+E2 occupancy is required to complete two concurrent PPIs and lock a P–E1–E2 “triangle.” No effector domains are included. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: Targeted Micro-C/HiChIP to quantify contact enrichment and 3D geometry; live-cell MS2 imaging and smFISH to extract burst frequency/size; no primary reliance on histone marks (ChIP is used only as a control to confirm absence of systematic changes). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6300980/?utm_source=openai))
- Controls: (i) single-site occupancy mutants (no assembly); (ii) pairwise-only bridges (P–E1 or P–E2) to test necessity of tri-point avidity; (iii) displacer peptide to transiently disrupt one PPI for reversibility. Positive control: dCas9-based inducible loop (CLOuD9) at the same locus to benchmark effect size. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: Step-like increase in P–E contact dwell time; increase in burst frequency >1.5× with minimal change in burst size; negligible global mark changes.

Aim 2. Convert the staple set into a local-rule grammar for multi-contact folding and quantify design–function transfer.
- Design: Expand to four to five “staples” using additional orthogonal coiled-coils to create a corridor that channels chosen enhancers to the promoter while insulating flanks, composing nested loops/sub-TADs. Layout rules (who-binds-whom) are the only variables; protein components are reused. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10361782/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: Capture-C/Micro-C to map intended corridors vs. spurious contacts; MS2 bursting; polymer-model-informed targets for contact probability vs. genomic distance provide quantitative expectations. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2151-x?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: Monotonic gain in promoter contact occupancy and burst frequency as correct staples accumulate; ablation of a minimal spanning set collapses the topology and expression.

Aim 3. Deploy to endogenous loci in human epithelial cells and neurons and demonstrate 3D→expression→phenotype causality.
- Target selection: Choose, per cell type, a gene with a validated distal enhancer and measurable phenotype (e.g., barrier integrity for epithelium; excitability metrics for neurons). Select 2–3 addresses per region based on accessibility and absence of coding sequence; install ZF–staples as in Aims 1–2. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41576-019-0128-0?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: 3D: Capture-C at target locus; Expression: nascent RNA by intronic smFISH; Phenotype: transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) in epithelial monolayers; multi-electrode array (MEA) firing patterns or calcium imaging in iPSC-derived neurons. Confirm that disrupting one staple acutely reverses both expression and phenotype. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41576-019-0128-0?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria: Pre-registered thresholds linking engineered 3D gain to burst-frequency increase and to phenotype shift; replication across both cell types.

Key design choices and justifications
- Orthogonal PPIs (SYNZIP toolbox) provide a scalable, addressable interaction alphabet with known geometries and low cross-talk, enabling multi-staple compositions without recruiting endogenous epigenetic modifiers. Splitting interfaces across addresses converts contact formation into a logical AND gate that suppresses off-target loops by requiring coincident occupancy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Reporter bursting as a primary functional metric is motivated by evidence that enhancer–promoter communication predominantly modulates burst frequency; causal manipulations of proximity therefore should primarily shift frequency, not size. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11058250/?utm_source=openai))
- Optional distance/orientation tuning: in a subset of constructs, insert de novo designed helical repeat (DHR) “rods” between ZF and PPI to test whether rigid nanoscale geometry further increases contact dwell time and effect size. DHRs offer length- and rigidity-tunable, genetically encodable rods validated structurally and mechanically. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/4845728/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and quantitative endpoints
- M1 (months 0–9): AND-gated 3-point bridge increases P–E contact dwell time ≥2× and burst frequency ≥1.5× in AAVS1 reporter; reversible by PPI displacer. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))
- M2 (months 9–18): Multi-staple grammar yields additive/nested contact patterns matching design; Micro-C shows intended sub-TAD-like insulation; expression scales with number of correct staples. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2151-x?utm_source=openai))
- M3 (months 18–30): Endogenous deployment meets pre-registered 3D→expression→phenotype thresholds in epithelial cells and neurons; acute disruption reverses effects within 24–48 h.

Validation of constraint compliance
- No catalytic epigenetic readers/writers are used; bridges are inert scaffolds. We will profile H3K27ac/H3K9me3 at target loci to confirm no systematic mark rewriting is required for the effect. Prior forced-loop studies (LDB1 tethering; CLOuD9; LADL) show proximity alone can modulate transcription, supporting our mark-independent premise. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5737898/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigation
- Risk: Some genes show weak correspondence between proximity and transcription (e.g., Sox2). Mitigation: pre-screen loci with CRISPRi/CRISPRa and Capture-C to confirm enhancer dependency; use multi-point staples to increase dwell time beyond transient “hit-and-run” contacts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/6534382/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Multisite targeting could still produce off-target bridges. Mitigation: choose ZF arrays with high-specificity motifs; AND-gating requires all addresses, dramatically reducing spurious assembly. Use orthogonality maps from SYNZIP sets to avoid cross-pairing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Mechanical strain or steric clash reduces efficacy. Mitigation: optional DHR linkers to tune spacing/orientation; iterate geometry based on Micro-C contact enrichment vs. predicted polymer distances. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/4845728/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental methods (selected)
- Protein modules: ZF-DBDs (16–18 bp recognition) fused via flexible or DHR linkers to split coiled-coils (SYNZIP1/2, 5/6, 3/4). Subinterfaces are designed to be weak alone and high-avidity in trans only when both enhancer and promoter addresses are occupied. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Genomic targeting: Lentiviral or CRISPR-mediated integration of ZF–PPI cassettes; gBlocks for ZF arrays; safe-harbor reporter with MS2 cassette and two validated distal enhancers.
- 3D assays: Capture-C/Micro-C; live two-color labeling of E and P for distance distributions and dwell times. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/19491034.2020.1782024?utm_source=openai))
- Transcription assays: MS2 live imaging; smFISH; RNA-seq for off-target expression surveillance. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6300980/?utm_source=openai))
- Phenotypes: TEER for epithelia; MEA and GCaMP imaging for neurons.

Expected outcomes and impact
- A generalizable, modular toolkit for causal control of gene expression through programmable, multi-contact chromatin topology, independent of histone/DNA methylation.
- A design grammar—akin to DNA origami staples but implemented with protein interfaces—linking local rules to predictable mesoscale folding and function.
- A validated pipeline for moving from 3D contact engineering to quantitative changes in bursting and cellular behavior in clinically relevant cell types. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9457169/?utm_source=openai))

References (selected)
- Genome organization and enhancer–promoter communication: Nature 2020; Nat Rev Genet 2019. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2151-x?utm_source=openai))
- Forced looping precedents: LDB1 tethering; CLOuD9; LADL/OptoLoop; BPCL chemical multiway contacts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4134511/?utm_source=openai))
- Orthogonal PPIs and designed geometry: SYNZIP toolbox; de novo DHR rods. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3339576/?utm_source=openai))
- Bursting linkage to proximity: reviews and live-imaging studies. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11058250/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Pinpoint-assembled transcription factories for locus-specific control of gene expression via covalently seeded, reversible mesoscale scaffolds

Hypothesis and goal
A covalently “pinned” nucleation hub at an endogenous promoter can seed a reversible, multivalent polymer shell that shortens local chromatin path length and concentrates core transcription machinery within ~100 nm, thereby increasing transcriptional burst frequency and mRNA output without relying on DNA methylation or histone modifications; dissolving the shell reverses the effect. The goal is to demonstrate a sequential causal chain—3D architectural change → target gene expression change → epithelial phenotype—at the endogenous CFTR locus in human airway epithelial cells.

Atomic strategy
Separate spatial memory from functional mass: use SpyCatcher–SpyTag covalent chemistry to fix a small geometric hub at the chosen DNA site (spatial memory), while allowing a noncovalent, signal-reversible polymer scaffold (functional mass) to assemble only around that hub. This scaffold provides multivalency and confinement to recruit Pol II/Mediator through IDR-dependent partitioning, not through chromatin mark deposition. Prior art shows: (i) locus-tethered condensates/LLPS can reconfigure contacts and modulate transcription (CasDrop, LAMPS), (ii) dCas9-mediated forced loops can regulate genes, and (iii) SpyTag/Catcher can recruit effectors to dCas9, but covalently pinned, geometry-coded, reversible “factories” at endogenous loci remain underexplored. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))

System design (PinFactory)
- Seed/hub (memory): dCas9-SpyCatcher targeted with 3–6 sgRNAs across a promoter-proximal window (−500 to +200 bp) and one nearby enhancer, to create multiple docking points. A trimeric coiled-coil “hub” bearing SpyTag ligates to each dCas9-SpyCatcher, fixing a nanoscale geometry with three orthogonal faces (valence = 3) for polymer initiation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10783489/?utm_source=openai))
- Polymer shell (functional mass): a soluble monomer carries (i) a head-to-tail, moderate-affinity coiled-coil interface for isodesmic, reversible polymerization only upon nucleation, and (ii) a synthetic low-complexity recruitment module (LC-Module; tyrosine/acidic-rich IDR lacking chromatin-binding domains) that partitions Pol II/Mediator by weak, multivalent interactions. Choice of LC-Module is guided by evidence that Pol II CTD, Mediator IDRs, and diverse TF activation domains partition into condensates and enrich initiation factors. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41594-018-0112-y?utm_source=openai))
- Reversible control: monomers include a rapidly inducible degron (AID or dTAG) and a protease-cleavable “breakpoint” in the polymer–polymer interface; auxin/dTAG triggers scaffold dissolution without changing chromatin marks, allowing on/off cycles. 
- Safeguards: no histone/DNA modifying enzymes are tethered. Tests will verify that activation persists when HAT/BRD inhibitors are applied, arguing primary action is architectural/kinetic rather than epigenetic.

Model system and phenotype readout
- Cells: primary human bronchial epithelial cells (HBECs) or 16HBE14o− monolayers at air–liquid interface.
- Gene: endogenous CFTR.
- Phenotype: CFTR function by Ussing chamber short-circuit current (Isc) with forskolin stimulation and CFTRinh-172 inhibition as ground truth. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8836180/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims and experiments

Aim 1. Build and validate PinFactory assembly and reversibility at an endogenous locus.
- A1.1. Genomic targeting and seeding. Deliver dCas9-SpyCatcher (lentiviral, EF1α) and sgRNA arrays tiling CFTR TSS and a validated proximal enhancer. Express SpyTag–trimeric hub (DOX-inducible). Confirm covalent hub capture by proximity ligation and ChIP for the Spy epitope.
- A1.2. Polymer growth confined to seed. Express polymer monomers (DOX). Readouts: (i) appearance of a diffraction-limited focus at CFTR (CRISPR live-FISH), (ii) fluorescence recovery (FRAP) consistent with reversible polymer dynamics, (iii) increased local concentration and residence time of Halo-tagged Pol II near CFTR by single-particle tracking. LLPS/partitioning rationale is supported by Pol II CTD and Mediator IDR behaviors. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41594-018-0112-y?utm_source=openai))
- A1.3. Reversibility. Induce auxin or dTAG to degrade monomers or express TEV to cleave the polymer interface, and confirm focus dissolution, loss of local Pol II enrichment, and return to baseline chromatin distances.

Milestones: >70% of CFTR alleles show seeded foci; Pol II dwell time near CFTR increases ≥2-fold; assembly/disassembly half-times <60 min.

Aim 2. Demonstrate causality: 3D architectural change → transcriptional bursting → mRNA/protein → CFTR function.
- A2.1. 3D architecture. Quantify enhancer–promoter distances and contact frequency by live imaging and targeted 5C/HiChIP (Pol II) with and without assembly; benchmark against forced looping systems (CLOuD9/LADL literature) but without long-range CID. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))
- A2.2. Transcription kinetics. Insert 24×MS2 into the 3′ UTR of endogenous CFTR by HDR (if feasible) or use intronic smFISH to extract burst frequency and size. Expect increased burst frequency upon assembly, returning to baseline upon disassembly. Locus-tethered condensate systems (CasDrop/LAMPS) support this directionality. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))
- A2.3. mRNA and protein. RT-qPCR and targeted proteomics for CFTR. Surface biotinylation to quantify membrane CFTR.
- A2.4. Phenotype. Measure Isc in Ussing chambers under forskolin ± CFTRinh-172. Expect ≥25–50% increase in CFTR-dependent current upon assembly; reversal upon disassembly. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8836180/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Exclude epigenetic primary mechanisms; test robustness across stimuli.
- A3.1. Epigenetic independence. CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag for H3K27ac/H3K4me3 and WGBS at CFTR before/after assembly. Expect no early (≤6 h) increase preceding transcriptional upregulation. Maintain activation under HAT (A-485) or BRD4 (JQ1) inhibition to the extent compatible with basal transcription, indicating the primary driver is architectural/kinetic, not histone acetylation.
- A3.2. Orthogonality. Confirm no genome-wide spread by RNA-seq; off-targets limited to sgRNA-bound sites.
- A3.3. Dissociation of loop versus factory effects. Compare to CLOuD9-like enhancer–promoter dimerization without polymer shell; expect smaller effects, isolating the contribution of the local factory. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))

Controls and falsification
- Non-seeding controls: monomer ± hub without dCas9-SpyCatcher; dCas9-SpyCatcher with scrambled sgRNAs.
- Recruitment-null monomer: polymerization-competent but lacking LC-Module tests whether geometry alone suffices; reduced effect would support a recruitment component.
- Positive control: light-activated LAMPS or CasDrop at CFTR to benchmark achievable Pol II enrichment and transcriptional changes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10065442/?utm_source=openai))
- Falsification: If 3D changes occur (contacts shorten) without transcriptional or phenotypic effects, the hypothesis fails; the system then acts as a geometrical tether only. If transcriptional changes occur without measurable 3D changes, revise the model toward kinetic partitioning as the dominant driver.

Readouts linking steps
- 3D change: live distance measurements; 5C/HiChIP (Pol II).
- Machinery concentration: Pol II/Mediator ChIP and single-molecule dwell times.
- Bursting: MS2 live imaging or smFISH burst inference.
- Output: CFTR mRNA/protein; Isc traces with CFTRinh-172 blockade. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8836180/?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcomes and interpretation
- Assembly increases local Pol II/Mediator occupancy and enhancer–promoter synapse dwell time, raising burst frequency and CFTR output; disassembly reverses all steps. This aligns with condensate-based enrichment of transcription apparatus at active loci while remaining distinct from relocating DNA to pre-existing nuclear bodies (CRISPR-GO) or using global optogenetic LLPS not covalently pinned (CasDrop/LAMPS). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6239909/?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility and novelty
- Feasibility rests on three established pillars combined in a new way: (i) locus-tethered condensates/LLPS alter contacts and transcription, (ii) CRISPR-mediated looping changes gene expression, and (iii) SpyTag/SpyCatcher supports robust, modular dCas9-linked recruitment. The novelty is the covalently pinned, geometry-coded, yet reversible polymer “factory” at an endogenous locus to drive architectural and kinetic control without primary reliance on chromatin mark editing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and timeline
- Months 0–6: Construct validation; in-cell seeding and confined polymer growth; reversibility tuning.
- Months 6–12: 3D metrics and live Pol II tracking; transcriptional bursting assays.
- Months 12–18: mRNA/protein and Ussing chamber phenotyping; epigenetic independence tests; comparative benchmarking to CLOuD9/CasDrop/LAMPS. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))

Impact
If successful, PinFactory establishes that directly rewriting local chromatin mesoscale architecture via a covalently anchored, reversible scaffold is sufficient to control endogenous gene output and epithelial function, without invoking DNA methylation or histone modification as the primary driver. This provides a generalizable, orthogonal route to program gene expression in epithelial and neuronal systems.

Project title
Mechanical rewiring of enhancer–promoter proximity with CRISPR-tethered magnetic nanoparticles to causally control epithelial and neuronal phenotypes

Hypothesis–question (merged)
Is calibrated, reversible, piconewton-range mechanical reduction of 3D distance between a defined enhancer–promoter pair sufficient to modulate transcriptional bursting and drive a measurable epithelial or neuronal phenotype, independently of DNA methylation and histone modifications?

Atomic strategy
Replace native loop-extrusion/architectural-protein governance with an exogenous, field-controlled physical variable: force-driven encounter frequency and dwell time between two targeted loci. The only intervention is distance/duration of contact; no recruitment of endogenous epigenetic enzymes or transcriptional activators.

Rationale and prior art
- CRISPR-based loop enforcers (CLOuD9, LADL/OptoLoop) demonstrate that synthetic contacts can modulate transcription, but they rely on protein–protein docking/oligomerization rather than calibrated mechanical proximity, limiting tests of “proximity sufficiency” and force–response maps. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))
- Magnetic tweezers and intra-nuclear micromanipulation have applied forces to chromatin and even to specific genomic loci in live human cells, establishing feasibility of controlled, piconewton-range nuclear mechanics. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1305265/?utm_source=openai))
- Live imaging of dCas9-Halo–labeled loci and nascent RNA reporters enables direct, time-aligned readouts of distance and transcription without altering chromatin marks. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7644657/?utm_source=openai))

Model systems and target loci
- Epithelial: Human immortalized keratinocytes or MDCK. Target a barrier gene whose output impacts tight junctions, e.g., CLDN1 (promoter) and a validated distal enhancer within the same or adjacent TAD.
- Neuronal: Human iPSC-derived glutamatergic neurons. Target BDNF exon IV promoter and a characterized activity-regulated enhancer.

Key deliverables and success criteria
- Demonstrate sequential causality with temporal order: induced distance reduction → acute change in nascent transcription → downstream phenotype. Early time points must precede detectable changes in local histone marks/DNA methylation.

Experimental plan

Aim 1. Build and calibrate a CRISPR–magnet system to mechanically converge two genomic loci
- Construct dSpCas9-HaloTag fusions and sgRNAs to the enhancer and promoter anchors. Label each bound HaloTag with orthogonally barcoded, biocompatible superparamagnetic nanoparticles (SNPs; 50–100 nm iron oxide; distinct fluorophores for two-color tracking).
- Hardware: Quadrapolar microfabricated electromagnet array beneath glass-bottom dishes to generate a centripetal field gradient that draws both SNP-labeled loci toward a programmed isopotential “convergence zone.” Calibrate force–distance with bead standards; operate at 0.5–10 pN.
- Structural readouts: Two-color live imaging of loci with dCas9-Halo dyes to quantify 3D separation and contact dwell time distributions (pre, during, post field). Validate with targeted Micro-C/Hi-C windows around the locus for population-level contact changes.
- Feasibility anchor: prior intra-nuclear magnetic micromanipulation of specific genomic loci in live human cells. ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Quantify transcriptional bursting as a function of mechanically enforced contact
- Knock in 24× MS2 stem-loops into the 3′ UTR (or first intron) of the target gene. Express MCP-GFP to visualize nascent transcription in real time.
- Protocol: Apply field pulses (e.g., 2 min on/3 min off) at graded forces. Measure burst frequency and size changes relative to matched no-field and nonmagnetic controls. Benchmark on/off latencies against distance trajectories to demonstrate proximity-first causality.
- Independence from epigenetic marks: CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag for H3K27ac, H3K4me3, H3K9me3, and DNA methylation (oxBS-seq) at 5–30 min after induction; require unchanged marks while transcription changes. Compare to optogenetic loopers (LADL/OptoLoop) as positive controls for contact-induced expression without mechanical force. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-019-0436-5?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Link transcriptional changes to phenotype with reversibility
- Epithelial phenotype: Transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER), tight junction continuity (ZO-1/E-cadherin immunofluorescence), and scratch-wound closure rate after transient field schedules that elevate CLDN1 transcription.
- Neuronal phenotype (extension study): Calcium imaging (GCaMP) and immediate-early gene dynamics (FOS/ARC smFISH) after transient boosting of BDNF IV transcription; assess synapse density markers if longer protocols are used.
- Reversibility: Far-field removal must relax distances, restore baseline bursting, and normalize phenotypes within defined washout windows.

Design details and controls
- Genomic targeting: sgRNAs avoid TF sites to minimize steric transcription-factor displacement; off-targets screened in silico and by CHANGE-seq.
- Nanoparticles: Zwitterionic or PEG-phosphonate coatings minimize nonspecific binding; chloroalkane-Halo ligand for covalent coupling; fluorescent barcodes for locus identity.
- Force-field schedules: Low-duty-cycle stimulation to limit heating and mechanoadaptation; temperature monitored at the culture plane.
- Controls:
  - Bead-only (no Halo/dCas9) under field.
  - Halo-labeled SNPs at neutral genomic sites under identical fields.
  - sgRNA-scrambled at one or both anchors.
  - Field-only (no beads).
  - CRISPR-GO periphery-tethering as orthogonal repositioning comparator (changes compartment, not pairwise distance). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6239909/?utm_source=openai))
- Artifact checks: Nuclear integrity (lamin A/C continuity), DNA damage (γH2AX), global transcription (EU labeling) to exclude stress responses driving the effect.

Readouts and analytics
- Structure: 3D interlocus distance distributions, contact dwell times, and Micro-C contact probability maps.
- Transcription: Real-time MS2 trajectories to extract burst frequency/size using hidden Markov models.
- Phenotype: TEER kinetics or calcium-spiking statistics aligned to stimulation epochs.
- Causal mediation: Time-resolved mediation analysis where the mediator is interlocus distance/dwell time; require significant average causal mediation effect and no early change in local chromatin marks.

Milestones and quantitative go/no-go gates
- M1: ≥40% median reduction in enhancer–promoter distance and ≥2× increase in contact dwell time during field-on epochs, reversible within 5–10 min off.
- M2: ≥1.5× increase in burst frequency with unchanged local H3K27ac/H3K4me3/H3K9me3 and DNA methylation at ≤30 min post-induction.
- M3: Epithelial TEER increase ≥15% or accelerated wound closure ≥20% within 24 h of daily 30-min stimulation blocks; reversal after cessation.
- M4 (extension): Neuronal calcium event rate or network synchrony increase ≥20% accompanied by elevated BDNF IV nascent transcription; reversal on field removal.

Risk assessment and mitigation
- Nuclear damage or heat: Limit forces <10 pN; monitor temperature; duty-cycled fields.
- Mechanotransduction confounds: Include LINC complex disruption controls; measure YAP/TAZ localization; focal adhesion signaling not expected to change in suspended monolayers.
- Inefficient locus labeling: Use multiple sgRNAs per anchor; validate occupancy by ChIP–qPCR for dCas9.
- Insufficient effect size: Target alternative enhancers with stronger baseline contact propensities; extend stimulation duty cycle while maintaining early epigenetic-readout windows.

Expected impact and novelty
This project tests the sufficiency of 3D proximity using a calibrated mechanical variable, not protein-driven dimerization. It establishes a force–structure–function map for specific genes and phenotypes with immediate, reversible kinetics and minimal reliance on endogenous epigenetic machinery. It complements and extends prior optogenetic loopers (CLOuD9, LADL/OptoLoop) and compartment re-positioners (CRISPR-GO) by directly controlling distance and dwell time through exogenous physics. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))

Key feasibility citations
- LADL and OptoLoop: optogenetic chromatin looping in mammalian cells. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-019-0436-5?utm_source=openai))
- CLOuD9: dCas9-based induced looping. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))
- Live intra-nuclear magnetic micromanipulation of specific genomic loci (proof of principle for force application to chromatin in situ). ([institut-curie.org](https://institut-curie.org/publications/live-cell-micromanipulation-genomic-locus-reveals-interphase-chromatin-mechanics?utm_source=openai))
- Magnetic tweezers in living cells (force scales and instrumentation). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1305265/?utm_source=openai))
- Live dCas9-Halo imaging of gene–enhancer proximity and nascent RNA. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7644657/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Coincidence-gated, pair-specific condensates to rewire enhancer–promoter communication in epithelial cells and neurons

Central question/hypothesis
Can we reprogram gene expression by enforcing enhancer–promoter proximity using a locus-pair–specific, condensate bridge that forms only when both genomic addresses are simultaneously occupied—thus converting phase separation into a coincidence detector that rewires 3D chromatin architecture without relying on DNA methylation or histone modifications as the primary mechanism? Prior work showed that recruiting phase-separating modules to single loci can nucleate local condensates and modulate chromatin and transcription, and that CRISPR tools can reposition loci or forcibly loop them, but none provide pairwise, logic-gated condensate assembly that only bridges a pre-specified enhancer–promoter pair. This project tests whether such logic-gated, pair-specific condensates can causally drive a sequence of effects: 3D architectural rewiring → transcriptional change → cell phenotype, across epithelial and neuronal contexts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10065442/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Encode an AND gate at the level of condensate assembly: design two sub-threshold, orthogonal multivalent scaffolds (A and B), each tethered to a different genomic address (enhancer or promoter). Neither A nor B alone phase-separates at its address, but A–B heterotypic interactions raise local effective valency above percolation only when both addresses are occupied within a genomic capture radius, producing a single mixed condensate that bridges the two loci and biases their contact probability. Pair specificity is enforced by designing A–A and B–B self-interactions to be weak/immiscible and A–B interactions to be strong/miscible. This leverages established rules that valency and affinity set phase boundaries and that interaction specificity can program mixing versus demixing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5703641/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims

Aim 1. Build a pair-specific, coincidence-gated condensate system (PairGate) and validate locus-bridging.
- Design: Two de novo coiled-coil–based scaffolds, CC-A and CC-B, each comprising concatenated heterodimeric CC repeats with attenuated homotypic interactions and strong A–B complementarity. Fuse each to a minimal oligomerization hub (e.g., trimeric/hexameric scaffold) to tune multivalency below the single-site percolation threshold; avoid IDRs known to recruit transcriptional machinery. Target CC-A via dCas9 to an endogenous enhancer and CC-B to its cognate promoter using validated sgRNA sets (5–10 guides per pad to create local “address arrays”). ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-43742-w?utm_source=openai))
- Prediction: No condensate at single pads; a single mixed CC-A:CC-B condensate appears only upon dual occupancy, coalescing the addresses into one phase-separated body that “wet-bridges” the intervening chromatin.
- Readouts: Live-cell two-color imaging of labeled loci (dCas9–orthogonal fluorescent tags) to quantify pairwise distance distributions and coalescence kinetics; acute induction of scaffold expression to map the temporal order of events. Quantify structural change with Micro-C/Hi-C^2 focused on the target region and by targeted capture-C before and after induction. Benchmark against single-locus condensate recruitment (CasDrop/LAMPS-inspired positive control) and against protein dimerization looping (CLOuD9) to separate condensate-bridging from simple tethering. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Demonstrate causality: structural rewiring → transcriptional change → phenotype in epithelial cells and neurons.
- Cell models and loci: 
  - Epithelial: human primary keratinocytes; target an enhancer–promoter pair controlling E-cadherin (CDH1) or keratin cluster gene with established enhancer contacts. 
  - Neuronal: human iPSC-derived glutamatergic neurons; target a validated activity-regulated gene (e.g., BDNF) with known distal enhancers.
- Temporal causality assays:
  1) Structure: track E–P approach and mixed condensate birth in real time; measure contact probability shifts within minutes by live imaging and within hours by Micro-C. 
  2) Transcription: MS2/PP7 nascent RNA tagging of the target promoter to detect burst frequency/amplitude changes within tens of minutes following bridge formation. 
  3) Phenotype: epithelial adhesion (calcium-switch aggregation, wound-closure migration) and neuronal excitability/morphology (patch-clamp firing thresholds, neurite length) at 24–72 h.
- Constraint compliance: do not fuse histone modifiers or transcriptional activation domains to scaffolds. Time-resolved CUT&RUN/CUT&Tag for H3K27ac/H3K4me3 verifies that early transcriptional changes precede or occur without significant mark changes, establishing that 3D architectural rewiring is the primary driver. Sensitivity controls with BRD4 inhibition (JQ1) and Pol II CTD kinase inhibition distinguish the architectural step (insensitive) from transcriptional machinery dependence (sensitive), clarifying the causal chain. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10065442/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Map design rules for pair specificity and universality across cell types.
- Interaction design sweep: vary CC-A:CC-B affinity matrix and repeat valency to locate the minimal parameters that yield pair-specific mixed condensates without off-target fusion, guided by established coiled-coil and multi-phase mixing principles. Use orthogonal pairs to target two E–P pairs in the same nucleus and test crosstalk. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-43742-w?utm_source=openai))
- Spatial gating radius: shift enhancer–promoter genomic distances (CRISPR-cut and re-ligation or selection of natural alleles) to define the capture radius over which coincidence-gated condensation can bridge loci.
- Universality tests: replicate best-performing designs in keratinocytes and neurons to assess whether polymer environment and baseline transcriptional condensates alter thresholds; compare with locus repositioning to nuclear bodies (CRISPR-GO) to separate pair-specific bridging from compartment tethering. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6239909/?utm_source=openai))

Key controls and falsification tests
- Single-pad controls: express only CC-A or only CC-B at their respective addresses; absence of condensate and no E–P rewiring falsifies nonspecific nucleation.
- Homotypic mutants: strengthen A–A or B–B to test whether loss of pair specificity increases off-target fusion; conversely, weaken A–B to abolish bridging.
- CLOuD9 tethering control: force E–P juxtaposition via rapamycin-dependent dimerizers without condensates; if expression changes are similar in magnitude but condensate-free, then condensates are not necessary. If PairGate yields distinct kinetics or amplitude, this supports a unique condensate-mediated mechanism. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms15993?utm_source=openai))
- Transcription-independent structure: in the presence of transcriptional inhibitors, confirm that mixed condensate formation and E–P proximity still occur, separating architecture from transcriptional output.
- Off-target genome safety: whole-genome 3D mapping (sparse Hi-C) to confirm no widespread compartment switching; RNA-seq to verify specificity of expression changes.

Quantitative success criteria
- Structural: ≥3-fold increase in E–P contact probability and ≥30% reduction in median E–P distance within 60 min of induction, with single-locus nucleation and CLOuD9 controls matched for targeting efficiency. 
- Transcription: ≥2-fold increase (or decrease, for “push-apart” designs) in nascent transcription burst frequency within 2 h, preceding detectable changes in H3K27ac/H3K4me3 at the promoter.
- Phenotype: statistically significant changes in adhesion/migration (epithelial) or excitability/morphology (neuronal) that are abolished by disrupting A–B complementarity.

Why this is novel relative to prior art
- Single-locus condensate recruitment (CasDrop, LAMPS) demonstrated local nucleation can modulate chromatin and transcription, but it does not implement pairwise, logic-gated condensate assembly to bridge a specific enhancer–promoter pair. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6724728/?utm_source=openai))
- CRISPR-GO repositions loci to nuclear bodies and CLOuD9 forcibly tethers pairs via dimerizers; neither encodes selective condensate miscibility to enforce pair specificity or coincidence gating that suppresses single-site nucleation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6239909/?utm_source=openai))
- De novo coiled-coil LLPS provides a tested route to orthogonal, programmable interaction networks that can be tuned for heterotypic mixing and homotypic immiscibility—properties we repurpose here to enforce single mixed-phase formation only between pre-specified loci. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-43742-w?utm_source=openai))

Feasibility considerations
- Interaction design space and orthogonality are supported by existing coiled-coil libraries with demonstrated LLPS and multiple orthogonal pairs in mammalian cells. Valency and affinity can be titrated to remain sub-threshold at single loci and super-threshold upon pair co-occupancy. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-43742-w?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanistic expectation that mixed versus demixed phases can be encoded by interaction asymmetry is established in synthetic and cellular condensate systems; bridging forces generated by protein–DNA condensates are sufficient to bias polymer configurations. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37996438/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and timeline (18 months)
- Months 1–6: Construct CC-A/CC-B libraries; calibrate sub-threshold single-pad behavior; identify working A–B pairs that form mixed condensates only upon dual targeting. 
- Months 7–12: Establish causality in keratinocytes at one locus; complete live imaging, Micro-C, nascent RNA, and epithelial phenotype assays. 
- Months 13–18: Port best design to iPSC-derived neurons; repeat full causal chain; complete universality and crosstalk tests; finalize design rules.

Outcomes
- A validated, generalizable method to rewire 3D chromatin via pair-specific, coincidence-gated condensates, with quantitative design rules for interaction specificity, valency, and genomic distance.
- Evidence that purely physical, scaffold-encoded condensate bridges can control gene expression and phenotype in epithelial and neuronal cells while minimizing dependence on endogenous epigenetic modifiers.

Title
Closed-loop temporal-interference neuromodulation to selectively damp stress-evoked sympathetic vasoconstriction in the uterus without systemic sympatholysis

Background and rationale
- Pelvic sympathetic efferents relevant to the uterus descend via the hypogastric nerves into the inferior hypogastric (uterovaginal) plexus, distributing along uterine vessels; this localization enables field targeting from the lower abdomen/sacrum. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK567711/?utm_source=openai))
- Norepinephrine contracts human uterine artery predominantly via post-junctional α1-adrenoceptors, so reducing burst-wise adrenergic release at this plexus should acutely relax uterine resistance vessels and restore perfusion. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2324242/?utm_source=openai))
- Human sympathetic outflow is organized into cardiac-synchronous bursts that increase in frequency and within-burst spike count during stress; high-frequency trains increase axonal vulnerability to conduction failure through Na+ channel use-dependent inactivation and extracellular K+ accumulation. This creates an intrinsic “burst-selective” weakness to subthreshold perturbations. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3273724/?utm_source=openai))
- Temporal-interference stimulation (TI) uses multiple kHz carriers to form a low-frequency envelope at depth with better tolerability in superficial tissue. TI has reached early human use and has also been demonstrated for peripheral nerves, supporting feasibility of extrapelvic actuation of autonomic fibers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11806287/?utm_source=openai))
- Uterine artery resistance/pulsatility indices are standard transabdominal Doppler endpoints; emerging wearable ultrasound patches can continuously track deep-vessel flow, enabling closed-loop, organ-specific control. ([obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/uog.12371?utm_source=openai))

Central hypothesis (question = goal)
Can a uterus-focused, closed-loop TI montage that remains quiescent at baseline but scales envelope amplitude only during Doppler-detected uterine vasoconstrictive episodes suppress stress-evoked sympathetic bursts in the uterovaginal plexus, thereby normalizing uterine vascular resistance without altering systemic sympathetic markers?

Atomic strategy
Exploit the burst-specific drop in axonal safety factor during sympathoexcitation: apply a deep-focused, subthreshold TI envelope over the uterovaginal plexus that slightly increases membrane polarization/accommodation only when bursts occur (detected via real-time rise in uterine artery PI/RI). This selectively increases conduction failure probability for closely spaced spikes, clipping pathological bursts while sparing basal discharge. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/physrev.00048.2009?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
- Aim 1: Field targeting and safety. Use individualized finite‑element models from pelvic MRI to design 3–4 electrode montages (bilateral lower abdomen, sacral triangle) with 3–6 kHz carriers and Δf 30–60 Hz that maximize the envelope along the uterovaginal plexus and uterine artery pedicles while minimizing fields in bladder/rectum and somatic nerves; verify skin current densities within established tES/TI safety limits and assess comfort in healthy volunteers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11806287/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 2: Physiology in humans (nonpregnant). Establish a standardized laboratory stressor (e.g., mental arithmetic with cold pressor). Primary endpoint: attenuation of stress-evoked rise in uterine artery PI/RI by active TI versus sham, measured transabdominally. Co-primary: no significant change in systemic sympathetic readouts (HR/BP, skin conductance) relative to sham. Exploratory: finger PPG amplitude and spectral HRV indices. ([obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/uog.12371?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 3: Closed-loop control. Integrate a belt-mounted ultrasound patch positioned over the uterine artery origin. Real-time PI/RI drives proportional TI envelope A(t)=k·max(0,PI(t)−PI0). Compare closed-loop to open-loop (same mean dose) for efficacy and off-target effects; quantify duty cycle reduction and baseline quiescence. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42191988/?utm_source=openai))

Methods overview
- TI hardware: Two or three independent current sources deliver kHz carriers (e.g., 3.2/3.24 kHz; optional third pair for steering). Initial current intensities set by modeling; envelope adjusted by controller. Stimulation blocks limited to ≤20 min, with thermal/sensation monitoring each minute. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11806287/?utm_source=openai))
- Target verification: Field maps co-registered to pelvic vasculature; montage tweaks guided by maximizing envelope overlap with the uterine artery/plexus corridor identified anatomically. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9321487/?utm_source=openai))
- Sensing: Transabdominal Doppler in Aims 1–2; wearable patch for Aim 3 provides continuous PI/RI with quality metrics and auto-site guidance. ([obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/uog.12371?utm_source=openai))
- Participants: Healthy, nonpregnant adults with regular menses; exclude implanted electronics, dermatologic issues at electrode sites, or pelvic neuropathies.
- Outcomes and statistics: Aim 2 primary analysis compares ΔPI during stress across active vs sham (mixed models, within-subject crossover; n estimated to detect 20–25% reduction in stress-evoked ΔPI with 80% power). Aim 3 compares closed- vs open-loop ΔPI and off-target symptom scores; report effect sizes and Bayes factors.

Mechanistic readouts (substudies)
- Cutaneous comfort/somatic recruitment thresholds during TI vs matched tACS to confirm superficial sparing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11806287/?utm_source=openai))
- Optional microneurography of peroneal MSNA in a subset to confirm no reduction in systemic burst frequency/incidence during active TI versus sham. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6146303/?utm_source=openai))

Risk management and ethical safeguards
- TI parameters remain within consensus safety guidance; continuous monitoring for heating and dysesthesia; immediate abort criteria predefined. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11806287/?utm_source=openai))
- Pregnancy excluded in early studies; separate obstetric safety pathway required before antenatal trials.

Success criteria
- Technical: Stable focusing of TI envelope to the targeted pelvic corridor with acceptable comfort.
- Physiological: Significant attenuation of stress-evoked rise in uterine artery PI/RI with preserved systemic sympathetic indices.
- Control: Closed-loop outperforms open-loop with lower duty cycle and zero baseline stimulation.

Why this meets constraints
- Non-invasive, uterus-targeted actuation via TI; no systemic drugs.
- Selectivity for excessive activation emerges from coupling actuation to uterine hemodynamic deviations and exploiting burst-state conduction vulnerability; basal tone is preserved.
- Novelty: No prior reports of TI directed at uterine or inferior hypogastric/uterovaginal plexuses; leverages established uterine α1-mediated vasoconstriction and validated Doppler endpoints with emerging wearable ultrasound for clinical translation. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2324242/?utm_source=openai))

Anticipated failure modes and contingencies
- Insufficient focusing/depth: adopt multi-pair steering and individualized montage optimization; if necessary, reduce Δf to shift focal maximum without raising superficial fields. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162641/?utm_source=openai))
- Off-target somatic activation: increase carrier frequency, reduce envelope depth of modulation, or move to asymmetric carrier amplitudes to cancel superficial fields. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40112352/?utm_source=openai))
- Weak Doppler signal (obesity, anatomy): guided placement with B-mode landmarks; if needed, switch to transvaginal probe for calibration sessions only, with subsequent patch operation matched to transabdominal targets. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4418013/?utm_source=openai))

Deliverables and milestones (24 months)
- M6: Validated FEM-based montage library for three body habitus classes; safety/comfort dataset in 20 volunteers. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11806287/?utm_source=openai))
- M12: Crossover pilot (n=24) demonstrating attenuation of stress-evoked ΔPI/RI with active TI vs sham.
- M18: Closed-loop prototype integrating ultrasound patch; controller validated on bench and in 10 participants. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42191988/?utm_source=openai))
- M24: Powered trial (n≈40) comparing closed- vs open-loop efficacy and off-target effects; dossier for IDE/IRB expansion.

References (selected)
- Inferior hypogastric/uterovaginal plexus anatomy and relation to uterine artery: StatPearls; pelvic dissections. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK567711/?utm_source=openai))
- α1-mediated contraction of human uterine artery; NE sensitivity. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2324242/?utm_source=openai))
- Sympathetic burst physiology and stress modulation in humans. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3273724/?utm_source=openai))
- Frequency-dependent conduction failure mechanisms in axons. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/physrev.00048.2009?utm_source=openai))
- TI mechanisms, safety, and human/peripheral demonstrations. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11806287/?utm_source=openai))
- Uterine artery Doppler endpoints; wearable deep-vessel ultrasound patches. ([obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/uog.12371?utm_source=openai))

Title
Closed-loop, state-gated, low-intensity focused ultrasound to evoke endothelial nitric oxide and locally suppress excessive uterine sympathetic drive

Integrated hypothesis–question
Can a uterus-targeted, rate-of-rise–gated, low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) stimulus that mechanically activates uterine/periuterine endothelium to release nitric oxide (NO) reduce excessive, sympathetically driven myometrial hypercontractility, while preserving basal uterine tone and systemic sympathetic functions? ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.1998.275.6.C1668?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit ultrasound mechano-transduction of vascular endothelium to produce a brief, spatially confined NO surge at the uterine wall/arterioles only when contraction kinetics exceed a pathological slope (high dε/dt). Local NO directly relaxes myometrium and presynaptically damps norepinephrine (NE) release at uterine neurovascular junctions, curbing excessive sympathetic activity without altering basal tone or non-uterine targets. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.1998.275.6.C1668?utm_source=openai))

Background and significance
- Uterine sympathetic outflow (via hypogastric pathways) and α-adrenergic signaling promote myometrial contraction and vasoconstriction; excessive adrenergic drive contributes to hypercontractility and ischemic pain. ([anatomy.ttuhscep.edu](https://anatomy.ttuhscep.edu/modules/pelvic_autonomic_module/pelvic_page11.html?utm_source=openai))
- NO potently relaxes human myometrium and contributes to uterine quiescence; notably, NO’s tocolysis in human tissue can be partly cGMP-independent, expanding mechanistic latitude. ([journals.physiology.org](https://journals.physiology.org/doi/full/10.1152/ajpcell.1998.275.6.C1668?utm_source=openai))
- Endothelium is ultrasound-mechanosensitive: low-intensity pulsed ultrasound increases eNOS expression/activity, intracellular Ca2+, and NO generation, producing vasodilatory effects without thermal injury. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1538783622157338?utm_source=openai))
- NO can inhibit sympathetic neurotransmission presynaptically (reduced NE release or signaling) in peripheral neuroeffector junctions, offering a local, non-systemic path to sympatholysis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3139802/?utm_source=openai))
- Ultrasound can modulate peripheral mechanosensitive channels (e.g., Piezo/TRAAK) and peripheral afferents, supporting feasibility of mechano-biased neuromodulation in end organs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9173751/?utm_source=openai))
- Pathological uterine activity is identifiable noninvasively; electrohysterography (EHG) and ultrasound strain analysis provide reliable contraction timing and permit estimation of dynamic features (e.g., slope). ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28649034/?utm_source=openai))
- Safety windows for diagnostic-range ultrasound and widely used LIPUS parameters (1.5 MHz, 200 μs, 1 kHz, ~30 mW/cm2 SATA) are well established and clinically translatable. ([aium.org](https://www.aium.org/resources/official-statements/view/prudent-use-and-safety-of-diagnostic-ultrasound-in-pregnancy?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Determine ultrasound parameter envelopes that maximize endothelial NO release in uterine-relevant endothelium while remaining within diagnostic safety indices. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39306482/?utm_source=openai))
2) Develop and validate a closed-loop controller that triggers sonications only when contraction rate-of-rise (dε/dt or dP/dt surrogate) exceeds an adaptive threshold. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28649034/?utm_source=openai))
3) Test whether gated uterine-focused LIFU reduces hypercontractile episodes and pain without altering basal uterine activity or systemic autonomic indices. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31303075/?utm_source=openai))

Study design and methods

Stage I: Mechanistic calibration (in vitro/ex vivo)
- Models: Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and, where available, human uterine artery endothelial cells (ex vivo). Outcome: NO (DAF-FM), eNOS phosphorylation, KLF2 expression; rule out thermal rise with needle thermistors. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26279754/?utm_source=openai))
- Ultrasound paradigms: Start with LIPUS canonical parameters (1.5 MHz, 200 μs, 1 kHz, Ispta ≈ 30 mW/cm2), vary pulse-burst envelopes (50–500 ms packet lengths, 0.5–2 Hz packet rate) to map NO dose–response; keep MI/TI within AIUM guidance. ([nice.org.uk](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/htg481/chapter/2-The-condition-current-treatments-and-procedure?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanism controls: Pharmacologic eNOS inhibition (L-NAME), Piezo1 siRNA in endothelial cultures, to test mechano-initiated NO. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0753332220309896?utm_source=openai))

Stage II: Proof-of-concept (rodent, nonpregnant)
- Preparation: Anesthetized rat; measure uterine contractility (serosal strain via high-frame-rate B-mode speckle tracking) and intrauterine pressure; place abdominal EHG electrodes. Induce sympathetic overdrive with systemic NE or α1-agonist microdose to create hypercontractile phenotype. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35389865/?utm_source=openai))
- Intervention: Transabdominal focused sonications targeted to uterine wall/perivascular regions using small-aperture 1–2 MHz array. Controller triggers a 200–400 ms LIPUS packet when dε/dt exceeds threshold; hysteresis to prevent chattering. Maintain MI ≤ 1.5 and TI within diagnostic bounds; log acoustic indices in real time. ([aium.org](https://www.aium.org/resources/official-statements/view/prudent-use-and-safety-of-diagnostic-ultrasound-in-pregnancy?utm_source=openai))
- Endpoints: Change in contraction slope, peak amplitude, and duty time; uterine artery Doppler resistive index; tissue NO (electrochemical NO sensor where feasible). Mechanism confirmation: repeat with L-NAME to test NO dependence. Off-target check: HR, BP, HRV LF/HF unchanged at rest. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1538783622157338?utm_source=openai))

Stage III: First-in-human feasibility (nonpregnant, primary dysmenorrhea)
- Design: Single-blind, sham-controlled, crossover in clinic. Inclusion: severe cramp episodes; exclusion: pregnancy, coagulopathy, implanted stimulators. Monitoring: EHG for timing and slope estimation; optional B-mode strain tracking for calibration. Sonications delivered only on excessive slope detections. Safety: MI/TI within diagnostic guidelines; exposure time capped by ALARA. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28649034/?utm_source=openai))
- Primary outcome: Area-under-curve of hypercontractile events per hour. Secondary: Pain VAS, uterine artery Doppler indices, lack of change in resting HRV LF/HF and blood pressure (systemic sympatholysis screen). ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK532927/?utm_source=openai))

Controller and sensing
- Sensing: Abdominal EHG array provides robust contraction onset and slope estimation superior to external toco; optional ultrasound speckle-tracking estimates strain rate for calibration. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28649034/?utm_source=openai))
- State gating: Trigger only when dε/dt exceeds an adaptive percentile relative to subject’s baseline, ensuring dormancy during normal activity and avoiding basal tone suppression. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0169260726002142?utm_source=openai))
- Patterned sonication: Short burst packets (200–400 ms) at 1 kHz PRF, SATA ≈ 30 mW/cm2; slight inter-packet jitter to limit adaptation; parameters kept within nonthermal ranges. ([nice.org.uk](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/htg481/chapter/2-The-condition-current-treatments-and-procedure?utm_source=openai))

Safety and risk management
- Acoustic indices monitored and enforced (MI, TI) per AIUM/FDA guidance; exposures minimized (ALARA). Avoid cavitation regimes; duty cycles and intensities in diagnostic/LIPUS range. Adverse event surveillance: skin/soft-tissue effects, menstrual pattern changes, vasovagal symptoms. ([aium.org](https://www.aium.org/resources/official-statements/view/prudent-use-and-safety-of-diagnostic-ultrasound-in-pregnancy?utm_source=openai))

Effectiveness tests and success criteria
- Stage II success: ≥30% reduction in pathological contraction slope and duty time versus sham; effect abolished by L-NAME. No change in resting HRV LF/HF. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3139802/?utm_source=openai))
- Stage III success: Within-subject reduction in hypercontractile AUC and pain VAS versus sham without changes in basal uterine activity between episodes or systemic autonomic indices. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31303075/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- Uses local, state-triggered endothelial mechano-NO as the actuator to downregulate sympathetic drive in a single organ, rather than systemic sympatholysis. To our knowledge, uterus-targeted, closed-loop, NO-centered, LIFU control of hypercontractility has not been clinically explored; existing pelvic neuromodulation is electrical or ablative, and prior ultrasound work emphasizes imaging, ablation, or non-specific physiotherapy. ([ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK567751/?utm_source=openai))

Clinical translation
- Hardware leverages diagnostic ultrasound platforms and adhesive EHG patches. Regulatory pathway aligns with non-significant risk device studies under existing acoustic output standards, enabling rapid iteration and controlled clinical testing. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/cdrh_docs/pdf17/K172056.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Contingencies
- If endothelial NO activation alone is insufficient, parameter sweeps will incorporate modest modulation targeting mechanosensitive ion channels in local afferents to augment inhibitory gating while keeping organ specificity and safety. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9173751/?utm_source=openai))

Deliverables and milestones (24 months)
- Months 0–6: Endothelial NO parameter map; thermomechanical safety characterization. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39306482/?utm_source=openai))
- Months 6–12: Rodent closed-loop efficacy and NO dependence. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1538783622157338?utm_source=openai))
- Months 12–24: Human feasibility (n≈20) with sham control; go/no-go for pivotal based on predefined success criteria. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28649034/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Closed-loop, uterus-derived-signal–gated low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) to suppress excessive sympathetic drive at the uterovaginal plexus while preserving basal tone

Rationale
- Convergent autonomic control. Sympathetic fibers via the hypogastric pathway and parasympathetic fibers via pelvic splanchnics converge in the inferior hypogastric/uterovaginal plexus before distributing to the uterus and its vasculature. This anatomical convergence creates a local control point for autonomic balance. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8500855/?utm_source=openai))
- Pathophysiology. Acute psychological or physiological stress elevates uterine vascular resistance and reduces blood flow via α1-adrenergic vasoconstriction; animal and human data link stress and catecholamines to higher uterine artery resistance indices (RI/PI). ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10253890.2016.1203417?utm_source=openai))
- Biomarkers. Uterine artery Doppler RI/PI and related waveform features are standard, noninvasive readouts of uterine vascular tone and can be trended continuously. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7409544/?utm_source=openai))
- Modality. Low-intensity focused ultrasound can modulate peripheral nerve excitability, with multiple reports showing reversible inhibition of nerve activity and mechanosensitive channel involvement, at acoustic exposures within diagnostic safety envelopes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8828880/?utm_source=openai))
- Unmet need and novelty. No noninvasive, uterus-specific neuromodulation exists that suppresses only pathologic sympathetic surges without systemic sympatholysis. Focused ultrasound has not been clinically applied to modulate the uterovaginal plexus for autonomic rebalance; prior uterine ultrasound applications are ablative (fibroids), and pelvic TENS/IFC trials address pain without closed-loop, organ-specific autonomic control. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43586-024-00368-6?utm_source=openai))

Unified hypothesis (research goal as question)
Can on-demand, low-intensity focused ultrasound directed to the uterovaginal plexus, gated by real-time uterine artery hemodynamic signatures of sympathetic overactivity, reduce excessive sympathetic vasoconstriction and myometrial hyperexcitability while preserving basal sympathetic tone and avoiding systemic sympatholysis?

Atomic strategy
Exploit activity-dependent susceptibility of sympathetic efferents at the plexus: deliver short LIFU pulse trains only during detected surges in uterine vascular resistance, biasing presynaptic and axonal mechanosensitive processes that disproportionately damp high-frequency, high-amplitude sympathetic output; remain inert at baseline.

Specific aims
1) Define uterine-local “excess sympathetic” signatures and thresholds
- Map individualized baselines and stress-evoked ranges of uterine artery RI/PI and waveform dynamics across menstrual phases in nonpregnant participants.
- Establish criteria for “excess” as deviations beyond personalized tolerance bands (e.g., RI percentile thresholds, rapid upslopes, diastolic notch re-emergence). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7409544/?utm_source=openai))

2) Establish a safe, selective LIFU parameter space for plexus-targeted suppression
- Using transabdominal or transperineal sonication geometry guided by B-mode imaging, focus within the known anatomic corridor of the uterovaginal plexus lateral to the cervix/uterine artery crossing.
- Parameterize frequency (0.5–1.5 MHz), pulse duration (0.2–5 ms), PRF, duty cycle, and intensity below diagnostic limits to maximize reduction of stress-evoked RI elevations while maintaining baseline RI within subject-specific corridors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8500855/?utm_source=openai))
- Primary selectivity test: compare effects on uterine RI/PI during standardized sympatho-excitation (mental arithmetic, cold pressor) vs resting baseline; verify minimal change in systemic markers (heart rate variability, finger PPG amplitude) to exclude systemic sympatholysis. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9888905/?utm_source=openai))

3) Implement and evaluate a closed-loop controller (“uterus-gated LIFU”)
- Sensing: continuous pulsed-wave Doppler of one uterine artery with beat-to-beat RI/PI estimation; optional redundancy with deep pelvic electrical impedance or optical perfusion.
- Control: state estimator computes real-time deviation from baseline; when excess sympathetic likelihood crosses threshold, trigger a brief LIFU burst; cease when RI returns to band.
- Outcomes: time-above-threshold RI, area under excess-RI curve, and variance reduction during stress tasks; maintenance of baseline RI and absence of systemic sympatholysis.

Study design
- Phase 0/feasibility, randomized, sham-controlled, crossover.
- Participants: healthy, nonpregnant women (18–40), regular cycles; exclude pelvic pathology and anticoagulation.
- Sessions: two visits in mid-luteal phase. Each visit includes baseline resting, two stress epochs, and recovery. Within each visit, deliver either closed-loop LIFU or sham according to randomization; cross over at second visit.
- Targeting: transabdominal ultrasound localizes cervix/uterine arteries; sonication focus positioned 5–10 mm lateral to cervix at the uterovaginal plexus region. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8500855/?utm_source=openai))
- Safety: acoustic outputs within FDA diagnostic limits; monitor skin, bladder, rectal symptoms; serial urinalysis; pregnancy test pre-session. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43586-024-00368-6?utm_source=openai))

Primary endpoint
- Percent reduction in excess sympathetic burden: AUC of RI above individualized threshold during stress with closed-loop LIFU vs sham.

Secondary endpoints
- Baseline preservation: mean RI at rest unchanged (noninferiority margin ≤2%).
- Systemic specificity: no significant change in HRV LF/HF ratio or finger PPG amplitude vs sham during stress. 
- Myometrial excitability proxy: change in pelvic impedance oscillation power in vasomotor band during stress.
- Safety and tolerability.

Mechanistic checks and falsification tests
- If LIFU reduces RI at rest, re-tune duty cycle/PRF to enforce baseline preservation; if impossible, ideation fails the constraint.
- If systemic markers change with uterine RI, include a “off-target focus” control 2–3 cm lateral to plexus; effect disappearance supports local mechanism.
- If responders cluster by cycle phase, incorporate phase as a stratification factor and explore hormone-level covariates.

Technical specifications
- Transducer: 0.75–1.0 MHz, f-number 1–1.5, focal spot ~5–8 mm; SPPA/Ispta below diagnostic limits; real-time beam steering within ±10 mm.
- Sensing: 3–5 MHz linear/curvilinear probe co-registered to sonication; Doppler processing at ≥100 Hz sample of envelope for beat-to-beat RI/PI.
- Controller: adaptive thresholding using rolling baselines; refractory windows to prevent over-delivery; safety interlocks on temperature rise estimated by acoustic modeling.

Validation pathway
- Bench-top phantom to validate co-registration accuracy and Doppler-driven triggering latency.
- Preclinical large-animal pilot (nonpregnant ewe) to relate sonication to uterine artery flow and catecholamine challenges. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10253890.2016.1203417?utm_source=openai))
- First-in-human feasibility as above; expansion to dysmenorrhea cohort if uterine hypertonicity and vasoconstriction signatures are demonstrated.

Clinical translation and risk
- Device integrates widely used diagnostic ultrasound hardware with a low-intensity neuromodulation module, facilitating regulatory path as a software-controlled therapeutic mode of an imaging platform.
- Known gaps: exact cellular mechanism of peripheral ultrasound neuromodulation remains under study; nonetheless, multiple studies show safe, reversible inhibition of peripheral nerves, justifying parameter exploration under strict safety monitoring. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8828880/?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
- Demonstrate ≥30% reduction in excess-RI AUC during stress without rest RI change and without systemic sympatholysis in ≥60% of participants under closed-loop LIFU vs sham.
- Reproducible targeting and safety across visits.

References (selected)
- Pelvic autonomic convergence and uterovaginal plexus anatomy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8500855/?utm_source=openai))
- Stress and catecholamine-linked uterine vasoconstriction, α1 mediation. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10253890.2016.1203417?utm_source=openai))
- Uterine artery Doppler as vascular tone readout. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7409544/?utm_source=openai))
- Low-intensity focused ultrasound neuromodulation and safety. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43586-024-00368-6?utm_source=openai))
- Prior electrotherapy for dysmenorrhea lacks closed-loop autonomic targeting (context for novelty). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11262556/?utm_source=openai))
