Title
Marrow-confined, replication-gated oncolytic adenovirus to restore MAC-grade graft-versus-leukemia under antibody-only conditioning in AML

Question/Hypothesis (undistinguished)
Can an intramedullary, leukemia-selective oncolytic adenovirus that locally expresses a CLL-1–directed T‑cell engager, a CD47 checkpoint trap (SIRPα‑Fc), and the CXCR3 chemokine ligand CXCL10 convert the leukemia-permissive marrow niche into a confined immune “hot spot,” thereby restoring or exceeding myeloablative-conditioning (MAC)–level disease control while preserving donor HSC engraftment and avoiding GVHD under non-genotoxic, antibody-based conditioning? This rests on three established premises: (i) RIC/NMA increases relapse versus MAC due to weaker cytotoxic/inflammatory priming; (ii) CLL‑1 (CLEC12A) is present on AML blasts/LSCs and largely absent on normal HSCs; (iii) oncolytic vectors can safely deliver BiTEs/checkpoint traps/chemokines for localized, multi-axis immune activation. ([astctjournal.org](https://www.astctjournal.org/article/S2666-6367%2821%2900718-1/fulltext?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Replace MAC’s systemic cytotoxic priming with a single, spatially confined switch: intramedullary, replication‑gated virotherapy that ignites multi-pronged, HLA‑independent, macrophage‑ and T‑cell–mediated GVL within marrow while leaving non-marrow tissues—and thus GVHD risk—unperturbed. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8411207/?utm_source=openai))

Rationale and background
- Relapse after allo‑HCT remains higher with RIC/NMA than with MAC across myeloid malignancies; the survival advantage of MAC often reflects superior relapse control despite more toxicity. The proposal aims to deliver MAC‑equivalent GVL without MAC’s systemic genotoxicity. ([astctjournal.org](https://www.astctjournal.org/article/S2666-6367%2821%2900718-1/fulltext?utm_source=openai))
- The marrow niche protects LSCs via retention and quiescence; effective targeting must work in situ. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/cancerdiscovery/article/9/5/OF11/42067/CXCL12-Has-Niche-Specific-Roles-in-Leukemia-Stem?utm_source=openai))
- CLL‑1 (CLEC12A, CD371) is present on most AML blasts and a majority of LSC‑enriched fractions but is not detected on CD34+CD38− normal HSCs—affording LSC selectivity critical for preserving engraftment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8457079/?utm_source=openai))
- Oncolytic vectors can express BiTEs, SIRPα‑Fc, and CXCL9/10‑CXCL10 to recruit and enable donor effectors while keeping checkpoint/anti‑phagocytic blockade local—mitigating the known GVHD risk of systemic checkpoint blockade post‑allo‑HCT. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/doi/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-17-2651/352753/p/Targeted-BiTE-Expression-by-an-Oncolytic-Vector?utm_source=openai))
- Intramedullary delivery and replication gating (tumor‑selective promoters; miRNA detargeting) are established methods to confine activity to marrow leukemia and spare HSCs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4852145/?utm_source=openai))
- Non‑genotoxic antibody conditioning (e.g., anti‑CD117/briquilimab) can enable engraftment without busulfan/TBI and fits the constraint set. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9118867/?utm_source=openai))

Study objective
Demonstrate that marrow-confined OV‑GVL achieves relapse incidence ≤ MAC while maintaining donor HSC engraftment and low GVHD under antibody-only conditioning.

Intervention: OV design, targeting, and gating
- Vector: E1A/E1B-competent oncolytic adenovirus (Ad5/Ad5F35) with AML‑selective replication (survivin/BIRC5 promoter or E2F‑responsive control of E1A) and miRNA detargeting using HSC‑high miR‑126 targets in essential viral transcripts to suppress replication in normal HSCs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6542078/?utm_source=openai))
- Transgenes (polycistronic, 2A-linked):
  1) Anti‑CD3×anti‑CLL‑1 BiTE for HLA‑independent T‑cell killing of CLL‑1+ LSCs/blasts. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/oncology/articles/10.3389/fonc.2020.599933/full?utm_source=openai))
  2) Secreted SIRPα‑Fc to neutralize CD47 locally and license macrophage phagocytosis and cross‑presentation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7053234/?utm_source=openai))
  3) CXCL10 to attract CXCR3+ donor CD8/NK/NKT cells to the marrow where the virus is present. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9450898/?utm_source=openai))
- Delivery: Intramedullary (femoral/iliac) injections into leukemia‑involved sites under imaging guidance 72–48 h before graft infusion to allow initial oncolysis/antigen release; a second dose at day +7 in high‑burden models if required. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4852145/?utm_source=openai))
- Conditioning: Anti‑CD117 (briquilimab/JSP191)–based, busulfan/TBI‑free platform ± minimal immunosuppression per antibody‑conditioning protocols; avoid systemic checkpoint inhibitors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9118867/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims and experiments

Aim 1: Engineer and validate marrow‑confined AML‑selective OV.
- Construct and test replication control (survivin/E2F promoters; miR‑126 detargeting) for selective lysis of primary human AML/LSC‑enriched fractions while sparing CD34+CD38− HSCs from healthy donors in 3D vascularized marrow‑on‑a‑chip and co‑culture with stromal cells. Endpoints: replication (qPCR), cytolysis, HSC colony formation, off‑target cytotoxicity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6542078/?utm_source=openai))
- Verify functional secretion/binding of SIRPα‑Fc and BiTE and expression of CXCL10; demonstrate enhanced macrophage phagocytosis of AML and T‑cell cytotoxicity in the presence of BiTE; note that OV‑encoded BiTEs and SIRPα‑Fc are validated modalities in prior studies. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/doi/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-17-2651/352753/p/Targeted-BiTE-Expression-by-an-Oncolytic-Vector?utm_source=openai))

Go/no‑go criteria: ≥2‑log selective kill of AML versus normal HSCs; no impairment of HSC CFU beyond vehicle; nanomolar-range BiTE activity; local (culture supernatant) but not “systemic” (media exchange reservoir) checkpoint trap accumulation in chip.

Aim 2: Define safe/efficacious intramedullary dosing and timing in vivo relative to allo‑HCT.
- Models: (i) NSG mice engrafted intrafemorally with primary human AML; (ii) immunocompetent AML models (e.g., C1498) transduced to express human CLL‑1 for BiTE engageability.
- Intervention: Intramedullary OV vs vehicle 72–48 h pre‑transplant; conditioning with anti‑CD117‑based antibody regimen (murine surrogate) without busulfan/TBI; then transplant allogeneic marrow and T cells (dose‑ranged to model clinical allo). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4852145/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: 
  - On‑target confinement: biodistribution (qPCR) shows marrow>>blood/liver/lung.
  - Engraftment: donor chimerism; CFU‑spleen; HSC homing.
  - Niche immunity: marrow CXCL10 gradient; influx of CXCR3+ CD8/NK; macrophage phagocytosis markers; absence of systemic cytokinemia.
  - Safety: GVHD scores/pathology; hematologic toxicity to donor HSCs.
- Rationale: Intratumoral/marrow‑local transgene expression mitigates systemic PD‑1/PD‑L1 blockade–associated GVHD risks reported post‑allo‑HCT. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39635535/?utm_source=openai))

Go/no‑go criteria: No delay in neutrophil/platelet recovery vs antibody‑conditioning control; GVHD not increased; ≥1‑log marrow AML reduction at day +21; virus confined to injected bones and draining marrow.

Aim 3: Efficacy versus RIC alone and versus MAC benchmark; mechanism of relapse prevention.
- Arms: (A) Antibody conditioning + allo‑HCT (control), (B) + intramedullary OV (test), (C) MAC (busulfan/TBI) + allo‑HCT (historical and small‑animal MAC positive control). Primary endpoint: 90‑day relapse incidence; secondary endpoints: OS, LSC frequency (limiting dilution xenograft), MRD negativity, GVHD.
- Mechanism: necessity tests with macrophage depletion, T‑cell depletion, and CLL‑1 blockade; rescue with BiTE‑negative or SIRPα‑Fc–negative virus variants to quantify contribution of each payload.

Success criteria aligned to research goal
- Relapse rate (and time‑to‑relapse) in Arm B statistically non‑inferior to or better than Arm C (MAC) with equal/less GVHD and preserved engraftment; Arm B superior to Arm A (antibody conditioning alone). ([astctjournal.org](https://www.astctjournal.org/article/S2666-6367%2821%2900718-1/fulltext?utm_source=openai))

Key design safeguards
- Target choice to preserve engraftment: CLL‑1 absent on CD34+CD38− HSCs reduces on‑target HSC toxicity risk; CD123 avoided for BiTE cargo due to known HSPC depletion potential. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/25/4/1358/9696/An-Anti-CLL-1-Antibody-Drug-Conjugate-for-the?utm_source=openai))
- Replication gating: survivin/E2F promoters plus miR‑126 detargeting to abort replication in HSCs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6542078/?utm_source=openai))
- Spatial gating: intramedullary delivery limits systemic exposure; supports localized chemokine and checkpoint‑trap gradients. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4852145/?utm_source=openai))
- Immunobiology: local SIRPα‑Fc and BiTE avoid systemic checkpoint/CD47 blockade that can provoke GVHD; CXCL10 focuses donor CXCR3+ effectors into marrow. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7053234/?utm_source=openai))

Statistical and operational plan
- Power: For murine relapse endpoints, n≥12/arm yields ≥80% power to detect 35% absolute relapse reduction (two‑sided α=0.05). Survival by log‑rank; competing risk for relapse vs NRM; GVHD grade by ordinal models.
- Manufacturability: Ad5/Ad5F35 backbone; payload size within adenoviral capacity; GMP‑compatible producer cell lines and purification.
- Safety monitoring: viral shedding PCR; anti‑adenovirus neutralizing antibodies; off‑target transgene in serum; stopping rules for GVHD, delayed engraftment, or systemic cytokines.

Contingencies
- Antigen escape: switch/stack BiTE against CD33 or dual CLL‑1/CD33 CODV; track with flow/MRD. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/2162402X.2021.1945803?utm_source=openai))
- Inadequate T‑cell recruitment: replace/add CXCL9 or IL‑15 “cassette” in the same locus; both are validated in OV platforms. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6951834/?utm_source=openai))
- Residual systemic exposure: tighten detargeting by adding additional HSC‑high miRNA targets; reduce infectious dose.

Milestones
- Year 1: Complete vector engineering; in vitro selectivity and function; marrow‑chip safety. 
- Year 2: Intramedullary dosing/timing and biodistribution; proof of preserved engraftment and low GVHD in allo‑HCT models. 
- Year 3: Head‑to‑head efficacy versus MAC benchmark; IND‑enabling tox (biodistribution, shedding, germline).

Anticipated impact
If successful, this marrow‑confined OV strategy provides a non‑genotoxic path to MAC‑grade relapse control by restoring multi‑axis GVL exactly where LSCs live, while maintaining engraftment and avoiding GVHD‑amplifying systemic immunotherapy exposures. It directly addresses LSC sanctuary, HLA loss, anti‑phagocytic signaling, and T‑cell exclusion through a single, local, programmable agent. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/cancerdiscovery/article/9/5/OF11/42067/CXCL12-Has-Niche-Specific-Roles-in-Leukemia-Stem?utm_source=openai))

Appendix: key evidence points supporting feasibility
- RIC relapse disadvantage vs MAC; need for safer GVL restoration. ([astctjournal.org](https://www.astctjournal.org/article/S2666-6367%2821%2900718-1/fulltext?utm_source=openai))
- CLL‑1 as LSC target absent on normal HSCs. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/25/4/1358/9696/An-Anti-CLL-1-Antibody-Drug-Conjugate-for-the?utm_source=openai))
- OV‑encoded BiTEs, SIRPα‑Fc, and CXCL9/10 validated preclinically; local expression mitigates systemic toxicity. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/doi/10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-17-2651/352753/p/Targeted-BiTE-Expression-by-an-Oncolytic-Vector?utm_source=openai))
- Intramedullary viral delivery is operationally routine in mice and translatable to targeted human marrow access. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4852145/?utm_source=openai))
- Systemic PD‑1/PD‑L1 blockade around allo‑HCT raises GVHD risk; local expression is preferred. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39635535/?utm_source=openai))
- Antibody‑only conditioning (anti‑CD117) offers non‑genotoxic engraftment platform compatible with the constraints. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9118867/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Remote, marrow-confined activation of donor HSC “effector-factory” circuits to eradicate AML leukemia stem cells without genotoxic conditioning

Central hypothesis
After reduced-intensity or antibody-only conditioning, donor CD34+ cells can be engineered with a heat-inducible secretory circuit and engrafted normally. Subsequent, noninvasive magnetothermal pulses confined to bone marrow will transiently switch on secretion of an AND-gated, myeloid/NK‑recruiting anti‑LSC engager, synchronized with local release of a CXCR4 antagonist to flush LSCs from niches. This spatially and temporally restricted pressure restores or exceeds the anti‑LSC effect of MAC while minimizing systemic toxicity and GVHD.

Rationale and prior evidence
- LSC sanctuary and immune escape drive post‑allo‑HCT relapse; HLA loss, checkpoint upregulation, and niche protection are frequent, arguing for MHC‑independent, niche-focused interventions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10640763/?utm_source=openai))
- CXCR4 antagonism (plerixafor) mobilizes AML blasts/LSCs from protective marrow niches and chemosensitizes disease in preclinical and early clinical settings, motivating timed, local mobilization during immune attack. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Clinically used SPIONs (e.g., ferumoxytol) accumulate in marrow macrophage-rich compartments, enabling local magnetic hyperthermia. Heat‑shock promoters (HSP70 family) can be activated by mild hyperthermia in vivo and controlled noninvasively (AMF or HIFU), providing precise on/off control of transgene expression. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3983192/?utm_source=openai))
- LSC-biased antigens CLL‑1 (CLEC12A) and CD123 (IL‑3Rα) are broadly expressed on AML LSCs and largely absent or lower on normal HSCs, supporting dual‑marker gating for selectivity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/7979301/?utm_source=openai))
- Antibody-only, targeted pretransplant conditioning against CD117 (c‑Kit) can permit engraftment without busulfan/TBI, aligning with the non‑genotoxic constraint. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1083879118309947?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Exploit remote, marrow‑localized hyperthermia to activate a dormant, donor‑HSC‑encoded secretory program only inside bone marrow, only after engraftment, and only during short pulses. Each pulse co-delivers: (i) transient local mobilization of CXCR4‑dependent LSCs and (ii) an AND‑gated, MHC‑independent engager that recruits NK/macrophage effectors and blocks CD47‑SIRPα during the window when LSCs are displaced and exposed.

Specific aims

Aim 1. Build and validate the marrow‑gated donor HSC circuit
- Engineering: Lentiviral vector in donor CD34+ cells with an HSP70‑responsive promoter driving secretion of a modular trispecific “LSC‑AND engager”: two moderate‑affinity binders to CLL‑1 and CD123 that must co‑localize to assemble a functional effector‑recruitment domain; a low‑affinity SIRPα variant fused to the scaffold to block CD47 locally (no Fc effector). The effector‑recruitment module biases NK/macrophage engagement (anti‑CD16 or FcγR‑tuned domain), avoiding pan‑T cell CD3 activation to limit GVHD.
- Engraftment first, action later: In NSG/NBSGW and humanized models, confirm circuit is OFF during neutrophil/platelet recovery and hematopoietic reconstitution, then inducible by brief marrow‑focused heating at 41–42°C.
- Readouts: promoter leakiness, induction fold, pharmacokinetics of secreted engager in marrow vs plasma, preservation of multilineage engraftment, and absence of off‑target cytokinemia. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5333050/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Achieve safe, spatially restricted hyperthermia and co‑mobilization in marrow
- Localization: Use clinically available ferumoxytol or bone‑tropic SPIONs (e.g., alendronate‑functionalized) to enrich iron in trabecular marrow; quantify biodistribution and marrow-to-liver ratios by MRI/MPI. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5505659/?utm_source=openai))
- Triggering: Apply alternating magnetic fields tuned to generate mild hyperthermia in SPION‑laden marrow (pelvis/sternum) for 10–20 min/pulse. In parallel, engineer SPION coatings for micro‑dose, heat‑triggered release of plerixafor to transiently disrupt CXCL12/CXCR4 retention.
- Readouts: MR thermometry, marrow‑restricted HSP activation, local vs systemic plerixafor exposure, blast/LSC mobilization kinetics, and maintenance of donor HSC niche function. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5333050/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Test LSC‑selective killing, immune‑evasion coverage, and GVHD sparing
- Models: AML PDX with documented LSC immunophenotypes and post‑HCT immune‑escape features; transplant with engineered donor CD34+ cells after antibody‑only anti‑CD117 conditioning.
- Interventions: Deliver magnetothermal pulses weekly for 6–8 weeks starting day +28 to +35 post‑HCT (after myeloid/NK reconstitution). Compare arms: circuit+SPION+AMF versus circuit without AMF, versus non‑engineered HCT; optional arm with systemic plerixafor to benchmark advantage of local release.
- Endpoints:
  - Primary: marrow LSC depletion (flow: CD34+CD38−CLL‑1+ and/or CD123+), MRD negativity, and relapse‑free survival versus controls.
  - Mechanism: depletion of HLA‑loss and PD‑L1high subclones (single‑cell genomics/proteomics), evidence of MHC‑independent cytotoxicity by NK/macrophages, blockade of CD47–SIRPα in situ.
  - Safety: donor chimerism, multilineage counts, absence of anemia/thrombocytopenia from inadvertent CD47‑axis effects, serum cytokines, and GVHD scoring; off‑tissue promoter activation by whole‑body bioluminescence or PET reporter. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10640763/?utm_source=openai))

Key design choices aligned to constraints
- No nonselective genotoxic conditioning: use anti‑CD117 antibody‑based conditioning and standard immunosuppression; no busulfan/TBI. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1083879118309947?utm_source=openai))
- LSC selectivity with engraftment preserved: AND‑gated dual targeting (CLL‑1+CD123) minimizes engagement of normal HSCs; induction begins only after hematopoietic recovery. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/7979301/?utm_source=openai))
- Overcome niche sanctuary: timed, local CXCR4 antagonism mobilizes LSCs from endosteal/reticular niches during each pulse, exposing them to effectors and engagers concentrated in marrow. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Counter immune evasion: MHC‑independent NK/macrophage recruitment bypasses HLA loss; embedded SIRPα module neutralizes CD47 “don’t‑eat‑me” signaling locally. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10640763/?utm_source=openai))
- Enhance GVL without exacerbating GVHD: avoid systemic T‑cell activation by not using anti‑CD3 TCEs; spatially confine activation and effector bias to innate arms within marrow.

Milestones and go/no‑go criteria
- Year 1: Demonstrate ≥20‑fold on/off inducibility in engrafted human CD34+ circuits without hematopoietic impairment; confirm marrow‑confined heating and negligible systemic cytokines. Go/no‑go: promoter leak <5% baseline; no cytopenias.
- Year 2: Show ≥2‑log LSC reduction and MRD negativity in ≥60% of PDX cohorts with three to four pulses; no excess GVHD versus controls. Go/no‑go: survival benefit and unchanged graft function.
- Year 3: Scale manufacturing and GLP safety (Biodistribution, AMF exposure margins, genotoxicity integration sites); prepare IND for first‑in‑human dose‑escalation in post‑allo‑HCT AML MRD+ patients using anti‑CD117 conditioning.

Anticipated outcomes and impact
This strategy converts engrafted donor hematopoiesis into a remotely actuated, marrow‑only anti‑LSC device. By coupling transient niche disruption with AND‑gated, MHC‑independent killing at the precise anatomical site of residual disease, it aims to match or surpass MAC‑level relapse control while avoiding nonselective, systemically genotoxic conditioning and limiting GVHD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4490031/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Marrow-targeted signal inversion therapy to eradicate AML leukemia stem cells under non-genotoxic antibody conditioning

Background and rationale
After reduced-intensity or nonmyeloablative allo-HSCT, residual leukemia stem cells (LSCs) persist by exploiting two dominant advantages: (1) niche protection mediated by marrow adhesion (for example, E-selectin–ligand interactions), and (2) layered immune evasion, including high CD47 (“don’t‑eat‑me”) and checkpoint ligand expression, while some relapses exhibit genomic HLA loss that abrogates donor T-cell GVL. In AML, LSCs and blasts frequently overexpress CD47 and can upregulate PD‑L1; E-selectin blockade dislodges AML from protective niches; and HLA-loss relapse is documented across donor settings. These data argue for a local, HLA‑independent, innate-effector–centric strategy that disables CD47- and checkpoint-based cloaking inside marrow and is paired with non‑genotoxic conditioning to preserve HSC engraftment capacity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2726837/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic hypothesis-question
Can we invert the meaning of CD47 and PD‑L1 on AML LSCs within bone marrow—turning them into pro‑clearance tags for donor innate effectors—while transiently reinforcing CD47 “self” on donor HSCs and opening niche space with non‑genotoxic anti‑CD117 conditioning, to achieve relapse control comparable to or better than myeloablative conditioning?

Core concept (signal inversion)
- On-target inversion on LSCs: localize a marrow-targeted, LSC-binding opsonin that simultaneously (i) blocks CD47–SIRPα to unmask existing eat‑me cues and (ii) converts PD‑L1 into an ADCC liability, thereby recruiting donor macrophages/NK cells independent of HLA presentation.
- Cis protection on donor HSCs: briefly augment CD47 “self” on the donor graft ex vivo to prevent bystander phagocytosis during the pro‑inflammatory window after infusion.
- Antibody-only conditioning: vacate HSC niches without systemic genotoxicity using anti‑CD117 (c‑Kit) antibody conditioning. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28061465/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Engineer and validate a bone marrow–tropic “Inverter‑Opsonin” that flips CD47/PD‑L1 meaning on LSCs.
2) Establish transient cis CD47 augmentation on donor HSCs to preserve engraftment under signal inversion.
3) Demonstrate, in vivo, eradication of functional LSCs and MAC‑comparable relapse control after non‑genotoxic anti‑CD117 conditioning.

Aim 1. Inverter‑Opsonin design, build, and in vitro validation
- Molecular format
  - Tri‑functional antibody fusion with: 
    a) LSC‑restricted binding arm (anti‑CD123 or anti‑CLL‑1) for specificity; 
    b) N‑terminal SIRPα ectodomain graft to locally block CD47–SIRPα at the LSC surface (a “licMAB”-like topology to overcome the CD47 antigen sink); 
    c) PD‑1 ectodomain or anti‑PD‑L1 arm fused to an ADCC‑competent Fc (afucosylated IgG1) to turn PD‑L1 into a kill switch. 
  - Fc engineered for high FcγRIIIa and C1q engagement to amplify ADCC/ADCP while avoiding systemic T-cell activation. 
  - Marrow targeting via a bisphosphonate tag to enrich drug in bone/mineral and reduce systemic exposure. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28061465/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanistic readouts in primary AML/normal HSPC co‑cultures
  - Binding hierarchy and selectivity across CD123+/PD‑L1 variable AML versus normal CD34+ HSPC.
  - Phagocytosis and cytotoxicity assays with human macrophages and NK cells (ADCP/ADCC), with and without IFN‑γ pretreatment to model inflammatory PD‑L1 induction.
  - Bystander safety: RBC agglutination/hemolysis and neutrophil phagocytosis assays to confirm sink avoidance and myeloid safety. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4739754/?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria
  - ≥10× increase in ADCP/ADCC on AML LSC‑enriched fractions vs normal HSPC; no significant RBC or neutrophil toxicity at ≥10× efficacious concentrations.

Aim 2. Transient cis protection of donor HSCs
- Approach
  - Ex vivo decorate donor CD34+ cells with a short‑lived CD47 ectodomain (or lipid‑anchored CD47 mimetic) that is shed/cleaved within 24–72 h, preserving early “self” signals during peak innate activation without long‑term niche effects.
  - Validate reduced macrophage uptake in vitro and preserved colony‑forming capacity and multilineage differentiation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/2775564/?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria
  - ≥70% reduction in macrophage phagocytosis of coated vs uncoated donor CD34+ cells in vitro; normal CFU output; loss of surface mimetic by 72 h.

Aim 3. In vivo efficacy under antibody-only conditioning
- Conditioning and delivery
  - Use anti‑CD117 (JSP191/briquilimab) to open HSC niches without busulfan/TBI. 
  - Deliver Inverter‑Opsonin intraosseously or systemically with a bisphosphonate tag to confine to marrow; optional single-dose E‑selectin inhibitor (uproleselan) to transiently disrupt vascular‑niche adhesion and expose LSCs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12443608/?utm_source=openai))
- Models and endpoints
  - Human AML PDX with limiting‑dilution LSC assays; compare four arms: (i) anti‑CD117 alone, (ii) Inverter‑Opsonin alone, (iii) combo, (iv) myeloablative control cohort (reference) in parallel experiments.
  - Primary endpoints: functional LSC frequency (extreme limiting dilution into secondary NSG), marrow MRD, and relapse‑free survival.
  - Mechanism endpoints: in situ macrophage/NK engagement, opsonin biodistribution in marrow, and independence from HLA by testing against HLA‑loss PDX or HLA‑downregulated blasts. 
  - Safety endpoints: donor HSC chimerism, cytopenias, liver enzymes, and systemic cytokines; GVHD scores (xenogeneic surrogate), with bias toward innate effector mechanisms. ([jitc.bmj.com](https://jitc.bmj.com/content/13/6/e011888.full.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- Success criteria
  - ≥1‑log reduction in functional LSCs vs anti‑CD117 alone; noninferior relapse‑free survival vs MAC control; preserved donor HSC engraftment and no excess systemic inflammation.

Key justifications anchored in prior evidence
- CD47 is overexpressed on AML LSCs; CD47 blockade restores phagocytosis and targets LSCs. Opsonization is potentiated when CD47 is blocked and eat‑me cues (for example, calreticulin) are unmasked. AML niches can be pharmacologically perturbed via E‑selectin inhibition to reduce sanctuary effects. These mechanisms are HLA‑agnostic and therefore retain activity against HLA‑loss relapse. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2726837/?utm_source=openai))
- AML‑restricted CD47 checkpoint inhibition via SIRPα‑grafted, AML‑antigen‑targeted antibodies (for example, CD33/CD123‑anchored “licMABs” or bsAbs) overcomes RBC antigen sinks and enhances phagocytic clearance. PD‑L1 can be converted to an ADCC liability using ADCC‑competent anti‑PD‑L1 or Fc‑engineered decoys. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28061465/?utm_source=openai))
- Donor HSCs physiologically upregulate CD47 during circulation to avoid phagocytosis; CD47 augmentation improves graft persistence without impairing hematopoiesis, supporting transient cis protection as a biologically matched intervention. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/2775564/?utm_source=openai))
- Antibody‑only conditioning with anti‑CD117 (JSP191) vacates niches with minimal off‑target toxicity and is in clinical testing, meeting the non‑genotoxic constraint. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12443608/?utm_source=openai))
- Bisphosphonate conjugation concentrates biologics in bone/mineral to increase marrow exposure and limit systemic spillover. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6037665/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental design highlights
- Protein engineering: produce a human IgG1 tri‑functional construct (CD123 binder–SIRPα–PD‑1/anti‑PD‑L1) with afucosylated Fc and a cleavable bisphosphonate linker for bone targeting; benchmark against CD123×SIRPα licMAB and an ADCC‑competent anti‑PD‑L1. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28061465/?utm_source=openai))
- Innate effector assays: ADCP with human M‑CSF macrophages; ADCC with IL‑12‑primed NK cells; titrate IFN‑γ to vary PD‑L1; quantify synergy of combined CD47 unmasking and PD‑L1–directed ADCC. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4739754/?utm_source=openai))
- LSC‑focused analytics: sort CD34+CD38− fractions for single‑cell RNA‑seq to track “inversion” signatures (CALR surface exposure, SIRPα pathway inhibition, FcγR engagement genes in local myeloid effectors). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/4126904/?utm_source=openai))
- Engraftment protection: coat donor CD34+ grafts with a recombinant CD47 ectodomain via lipid tail insertion; track mimetic decay kinetics and macrophage uptake; validate that coating is absent by day 3 post‑infusion. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/2775564/?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo: intraosseous versus IV dosing comparison for marrow AUC; add a single peri‑dosing uproleselan injection in an exploratory cohort to test whether brief adhesion disruption further exposes LSCs without harming donor HSC lodgment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11017789/?utm_source=openai))

Risk mitigation
- RBC/neutrophil toxicity: AML‑antigen anchoring reduces off‑target CD47 blockade; screen for hemagglutination and neutropenia in vitro before in vivo dosing. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28061465/?utm_source=openai))
- PD‑L1 variability: efficacy must not depend on PD‑L1; CD47 inversion alone should drive ADCP; PD‑L1 arm is additive where expressed. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2726837/?utm_source=openai))
- Over‑activation/GVHD: innate‑biased effector recruitment via Fc avoids direct T‑cell engagement; monitor cytokines and add dose‑titration to maintain marrow‑localized activity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4739754/?utm_source=openai))
- Bone targeting sufficiency: if bisphosphonate targeting is inadequate, pivot to intraosseous administration to ensure marrow confinement. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6037665/?utm_source=openai))

Benchmarks and outcomes
- Primary efficacy benchmark: In AML PDX, combo (Inverter‑Opsonin + anti‑CD117) achieves functional LSC frequency ≤ that seen after MAC control and prolongs relapse‑free survival without increased systemic toxicity. 
- Translational readiness: GLP tox with marrow accumulation, RBC safety margin, and no off‑target organ deposition; manufacturing feasibility of tri‑functional format established.

Impact
This study operationalizes a single systems‑level perturbation—signal inversion of CD47/PD‑L1 on LSCs—paired with antibody‑only niche opening to deliver HLA‑independent, marrow‑confined clearance of LSCs while protecting donor HSCs. If successful, it reframes conditioning from systemic ablation to local immune‑mechanics, aiming for MAC‑level relapse control without non‑selective genotoxicity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2726837/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Niche-conditional metabolic disarming with donor memory-like NK cells as non-genotoxic “biologic conditioning” to eradicate leukemia stem cells prior to allogeneic HSCT

Rationale and significance
- Reduced-intensity/nonmyeloablative (RIC/NMA) regimens lower toxicity but leave residual AML leukemia stem cells (LSCs) protected within bone marrow niches by CXCL12–CXCR4 retention and adhesion via VLA-4/VCAM-1 and E-selectin, promoting relapse. Targeting E-selectin or CXCR4 can mobilize/leverage this niche dependency. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4713889/?utm_source=openai))
- Donor cytokine-induced memory-like NK (ML NK) cells (ex vivo IL‑12/15/18) show antileukemic activity with functional persistence and low GVHD risk after allo-HCT, and can compensate for the weaker cytoreductive effect of RIC/NMA. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9210521/?utm_source=openai))
- Two immunosuppressive metabolites—adenosine and kynurenine—are enriched in hypoxic marrow; adenosine via A2A/A2B receptors and kynurenine via AhR signaling blunt NK/T-cell function and drive checkpoint programs (for example PD‑1 upregulation), respectively. Enzymatic depletion of either metabolite restores antitumor immunity in preclinical models. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6218627/?utm_source=openai))
- Targeted desialylation at the immune synapse unmasks cancer cells to innate effectors by disrupting inhibitory Siglec–sialoglycan interactions and enhances cytolysis; antibody/BiTE–sialidase fusions validate this principle in vivo. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41589-020-0622-x?utm_source=openai))
- Anti‑CD117 (c‑Kit) antibody conditioning opens marrow niches without genotoxic injury and has entered early clinical testing in MDS/AML, enabling donor HSC engraftment. ([clinicaltrials.gov](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04429191?cond=%28LEUKEMIA%2C+ACUTE+MYELOID%29+OR+%28TERT+OR+PICALM+OR+FLT3+OR+DNMT3A+OR+SH3GL1+OR+KIT+OR+NPM1+OR+LPP+OR+JAK2+OR+KRAS+OR+NUP214+OR+CHIC2+OR+ETV6+OR+CEBPA+OR+GATA2+OR+RUNX1+OR+AF10%29&rank=5&utm_source=openai))

Central question/hypothesis
Can pre-transplant, marrow-restricted enzymatic collapse of adenosine/kynurenine fields coupled to NK effector engagement eradicate LSCs and restore donor anti-leukemia immunity (GVL) under RIC/NMA without increasing GVHD or impairing donor HSC engraftment?

Atomic strategy
Exploit the marrow niche itself as an activation switch: deliver donor ML NK cells that activate only in hypoxic, protease-enriched marrow and, upon target engagement, locally deplete adenosine and kynurenine while modestly desialylating the leukemia surface—converting three independent evasion axes into liabilities—then proceed to allo-HSCT supported by non-genotoxic niche opening.

Specific aims

Aim 1. Build and validate “Niche-Disarming ML NK” (ND-ML NK) engineered for marrow-restricted metabolic editing and synapse-localized innate checkpoint relief.
- Design: Haploidentical donor ML NKs expressing: (a) membrane-anchored ADA2 variant and secretable kynureninase under a hypoxia-responsive promoter (HRE/ODD) to restrict activity to low-O2 marrow; (b) a low-activity, synapse-tethered human sialidase module activated by tumor-associated proteases (masking peptide with MMP/ADAM-cleavable linker) to minimally remove trans sialoglycans at the NK–LSC interface; and (c) safety iCasp9.
- In vitro models: Human AML LSC-enriched CD34+CD38− fractions with human MSC/endothelium co-culture on VCAM‑1/E‑selectin substrates under hypoxia vs normoxia. Readouts: pericellular adenosine/kynurenine kinetics, NK degranulation/cytotoxicity, T/NK checkpoint programs (A2A/A2B target genes; PD‑1/PD‑L1 transcription downstream of AhR), LSC frequency by limiting dilution. Expected outcome: hypoxia-gated ADA2/kynureninase lowers adenosine/kynurenine, restores NK activation, and reduces LSC frequency; masked sialidase enhances synapse quality and killing without broad desialylation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Overcome marrow sanctuary in vivo and quantify LSC eradication and donor engraftment compatibility.
- Models: (i) NSG AML PDX with intraosseous disease; (ii) immunocompetent AML models for niche biology. Interventions: RIC/NMA baseline ± ND‑ML NK (intrabone or targeted IV) with timed plerixafor or E-selectin inhibitor uproleselan to transiently dislodge LSCs; compare ± anti‑CD117 (JSP191/briquilimab) non-genotoxic niche opening. Endpoints: marrow metabolite profiling, LSC frequency by serial transplantation, MRD, ND‑ML NK persistence, donor CD34+ engraftment after subsequent allo‑HCT, GVHD scoring. Success criterion: ≥1-log LSC reduction and superior post‑HCT relapse-free survival vs RIC/NMA alone, with preserved donor HSC engraftment and no GVHD increase. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7184728/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Translational pilot in high-risk AML undergoing haploidentical allo-HSCT with RIC/NMA.
- Design: Single-arm, dose-escalation ND-ML NK on day −5 (intraosseous preferred), plerixafor or uproleselan on day −4 to mobilize niche-protected LSCs, anti‑CD117 on day −7 to open niches; donor graft on day 0; no busulfan/TBI. Primary endpoints: safety (DLTs, cytopenias, infections), aGVHD grade II–IV and cGVHD. Secondary: MRD negativity pre‑HCT, day +30/+100 donor chimerism, 1‑year relapse incidence vs institutional MAC historical controls. Correlatives: marrow adenosine/kynurenine levels, transcriptional A2A/AhR checkpoint signatures, sialoglycan density on residual blasts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11017789/?utm_source=openai))

Key design choices and justifications
- Why NK lineage: Alloreactive NK and ML NK provide GVL with low GVHD liability and persist after transfer, fitting the mandate to enhance GVL without exacerbating GVHD. Missing‑self recognition also covers HLA‑loss variants common in AML escape. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9210521/?utm_source=openai))
- Why metabolic disarming: Enzymatic depletion turns diffusible, niche-sustaining suppressors (adenosine, kynurenine) into actionable targets; ADA2/kynureninase efficacy is established preclinically, and hypoxia-gated expression confines action to marrow to spare peripheral tissues and normal HSCs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9206478/?utm_source=openai))
- Why mild, synapse-localized desialylation: Targeted removal of sialoglycans at the immune synapse breaks Siglec-mediated brakes and augments innate cytotoxicity without systemic desialylation. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41589-020-0622-x?utm_source=openai))
- Why RIC-compatible niche access: Transient CXCR4/E‑selectin disruption dislodges LSCs and sensitizes them, while anti‑CD117 opens space for donor HSCs without genotoxic injury, meeting the constraint to avoid busulfan/TBI. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7184728/?utm_source=openai))

Methods overview
- Cell engineering: GMP-grade haploidentical ND-ML NKs generated from the donor, IL‑12/15/18 priming, lentiviral constructs with HRE–ADA2/kynureninase and protease-masked human sialidase; iCasp9 safety switch.
- Spatial control: intraosseous infusion to maximize marrow exposure; hypoxia-inducible expression validated in vitro and by reporter imaging in vivo. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- Pharmacology: timed plerixafor or uproleselan; single-dose anti‑CD117 per existing dose-finding data. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11017789/?utm_source=openai))
- Analytics: targeted LC–MS of adenosine/kynurenine in marrow aspirates; single-cell RNA-seq for A2A/AhR target signatures; flow cytometry of NK checkpoints; leukemia stem cell frequency by limiting dilution/serial transplantation.

Safety and risk mitigation
- On-target marrow editing is spatially restricted (intraosseous route; HRE gating) with suicide switch control. Titrate enzymatic payload to avoid excessive interference with donor HSC homing; perform staged infusion (ND‑ML NK on day −5; donor HSCs on day 0 after metabolic field normalization). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- Monitor GVHD and cytokine profiles; NK products selected/expanded to minimize contaminating T cells; no systemic genotoxins.

Decision gates
- Go/no-go after Aim 1: ≥3× increase in NK cytotoxicity against LSC-enriched targets under hypoxia with ≥50% reduction in pericellular adenosine and kynurenine vs control.
- Go/no-go after Aim 2: ≥1-log LSC reduction and unchanged engraftment kinetics vs RIC alone; no increase in GVHD signals.
- Clinical pilot success: ≤20% DLT rate; MRD negativity ≥50% pre‑HCT; 1‑year relapse ≤ MAC historical benchmark.

Impact
By converting marrow niche biochemistry into a selective activation switch and locally dismantling the metabolite fields that enforce immune tolerance, ND‑ML NK “biologic conditioning” directly addresses LSC sanctuary and multi-axis immune evasion, compensating for reduced cytoreduction under RIC/NMA while preserving donor HSC engraftment and minimizing GVHD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9210521/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Rate-thresholded niche-expulsion to eradicate AML leukemia stem cells during RIC/NMA allo-HSCT

Central hypothesis-question
Can we replace myeloablative cytotoxicity with a marrow-confined, rate-thresholded oxidative “ambush” that is triggered by LSC-specific adhesion forces at the niche boundary, such that the act of leaving the niche pushes LSC antioxidant systems past their kinetic buffering limits and yields selective immunogenic clearance without impairing donor HSC engraftment?

Atomic strategy
Exploit a kinetic disparity: AML LSCs sustain higher mitochondrial throughput and depend on rapid peroxiredoxin/thioredoxin cycling to keep ROS low; when ROS production rate briefly exceeds their detox capacity (hyperoxidation “floodgate”), LSCs fail while quiescent, glycolysis-biased HSCs remain below the same rate threshold. Engineer VLA-4–tension-gated carriers that convert high-affinity/force adhesion—enriched on LSCs in CXCL12/VCAM-1 niches—into a local, ultra-short redox pulse precisely at detachment, when pO2 and Ca2+ transients amplify ROS, and couple this with marrow-confined anti-CD47 to convert resultant damage-associated signals into focused GVL without systemic activation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/9890038/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims

Aim 1. Calibrate LSC vs HSC redox rate thresholds at niche exit.
- Question: What instantaneous H2O2/lipid-ROS production rates during detachment and O2 upshift hyperoxidize peroxiredoxins in primary AML LSCs but not in matched HSCs?
- Approach:
  - Microfluidic marrow-mimetic with tunable CXCL12 gradients, VCAM-1 surfaces, and controlled O2 steps (10–30 mm Hg) to emulate marrow-to-blood transition. Live imaging of mitochondrial ROS (MitoSOX), lipid peroxidation (BODIPY 581/591 C11), and peroxiredoxin hyperoxidation (Prx-SO2/3 immunoblots) in FACS-purified LSCs vs CD34+CD38− HSCs. Quantify cell-cycle entry–linked ROS overshoots in LSCs. Determine d(ROS)/dt thresholds that cause irreversible Prx hyperoxidation and death. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24590072/?utm_source=openai))
  - Define safety margins where HSCs (glycolysis-favoring, quiescent) remain subthreshold. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9056110/?utm_source=openai))
- Go/no-go: Proceed if LSC lethal threshold is ≥1.5× lower than HSC under matched pulses, with ≥20% absolute viability separation at 24 h.

Aim 2. Build VLA-4–tension-gated niche-expellers that deliver instantaneous, marrow-confined redox pulses.
- Question: Can integrin-force histories unique to LSC–niche adhesion be used to trigger a microburst of ROS and gradient collapse only where LSCs detach?
- Device concept:
  - Force-gated ligand-carriers: DNA hairpin mechanoswitches (tunable 4–19 pN) presenting high-affinity α4β1 ligands. Under sustained LSC-range VLA-4 tension, hairpins unfold to: (i) release a rapidly cleared, short-radius redox amplifier (e.g., membrane-impermeant H2O2 microburst via encapsulated glucose oxidase/catalase ratio tuned for sub-second spikes), and (ii) co-release a CXCL12 decoy to locally collapse the retention gradient, converting “attach” into “expel.” Hairpins re-close below threshold, limiting bystander activation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4209443/?utm_source=openai))
  - Add a shear-exposed mask that unmasks a tethered anti-CD47 scFv only after detachment and entry into sinusoidal shear, restricting phagocytosis enhancement to newly mobilized cells. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/21/16/3597/117531/Molecular-Pathways-Activating-T-Cells-after-Cancer?utm_source=openai))
- In vitro tests:
  - Co-culture AML LSCs or blasts with human mesenchymal stromal cells on VCAM-1, CXCL12 matrices. Apply physiologic force/flow. Readouts: carrier activation maps, local H2O2 profiles (HyPer7), Prx hyperoxidation, viability, detachment kinetics; phagocytosis by human macrophages/DCs with and without the shear-unmasked anti-CD47. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6356639/?utm_source=openai))
- Criteria for advancement: ≥2× selectivity index (LSC kill/HSC kill) at equal carrier dose; negligible stromal cytotoxicity; anti-CD47 activity confined to detached-cell ROIs.

Aim 3. Demonstrate LSC eradication and preserved engraftment in RIC/NMA allo-HSCT models.
- Model: NSG mice bearing primary human AML PDX with LSC quantification by limiting dilution; parallel syngeneic mouse AML for immune readouts. Conditioning: RIC/NMA analogue. Interventions: (1) carriers i.v. + intraosseous infusion for marrow enrichment; (2) 30–60 min later, transient systemic glucose pulse to fuel GOx microbursts without sustained oxidant load; (3) immediate donor graft infusion. Control arms: RIC alone; RIC + plerixafor; RIC + systemic anti-CD47. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0145212620301478?utm_source=openai))
- Endpoints:
  - Primary: frequency of functional LSCs (secondary transplant), relapse-free survival versus MAC historical controls; chimerism/engraftment kinetics to ensure HSC function. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4201264/?utm_source=openai))
  - Mechanism: marrow-confined Prx-SO2/3 in LSCs; DAMPs/ICD markers; DC cross-priming; NK activation vs HLA status; absence of systemic oxidative damage. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4749870/?utm_source=openai))
  - Safety: GVHD scoring; cytokines; stromal integrity; off-target hematopoiesis suppression.

Study design and methods

1) Cell sources and sorting
- AML: diagnostic bone marrow samples, enrich LSCs by CD34+CD38− or patient-specific LSC phenotype; normal HSCs from healthy donors. Parallel assessment of α4β1 activation levels and CXCR4 expression to validate higher-tension adhesion propensity in AML. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6356639/?utm_source=openai))

2) Mechanotransduction platform
- DNA-hairpin force gates assembled on liposomal or polymer carriers with α4β1 ligands; F1/2 tuned to 9–15 pN to bias toward high-affinity VLA-4 states. Fluorogenic readout reports cumulative force exposure and cargo release. Validate gating and cumulative-memory behavior. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6087633/?utm_source=openai))

3) Redox pulse engineering
- Encapsulate a stoichiometrically constrained GOx/catalase pair or photo-redox dye that yields sub-second H2O2 spikes with <10 µm diffusion radius; confirm microburst profiles in marrow-like gels using HyPer7 and Amplex UltraRed. Link kinetics to Prx hyperoxidation inflection determined in Aim 1. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4749870/?utm_source=openai))

4) Niche-expulsion module
- Co-pack CXCL12-decoy (high-affinity CXCR4-binding protein) released on the same force gate to locally flatten CXCL12 gradients and reduce inside-out α4β1 affinity, converting adhesion to detachment. Compare with plerixafor mobilization as benchmark. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7499473/?utm_source=openai))

5) Immune amplification without systemic activation
- Anti-CD47 scFv is tethered under a shear-cleavable mask so that exposure occurs only post-detachment in sinusoidal flow; assess macrophage/DC phagocytosis and cross-priming, NK-mediated killing of HLA-deficient variants, and T-cell responses after donor engraftment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4598283/?utm_source=openai))

6) Transplant protocols
- Timing: administer carriers 12–24 h pre-graft during RIC/NMA; allow >6 h for payload decay; infuse donor graft. Monitor donor chimerism, lineage reconstitution, GVHD. Use RIC to lower nonrelapse mortality but compensate anti-leukemia effect via LSC-targeted kill and focused GVL. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7378925/?utm_source=openai))

Key outcome measures and analyses
- Selectivity: LSC vs HSC viability (Annexin V/7-AAD), colony-forming assays, and long-term repopulation of normal HSCs in NSG. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9056110/?utm_source=openai))
- Kinetics: single-cell Prx-SO2/3, ROS bursts, and time-locked detachment events relative to force-gate opening and O2 upshift.
- Leukemia control: reduction in LSC frequency by ELDA; relapse-free survival compared with RIC and MAC historical benchmarks; sensitivity analyses across AML genotypes.
- Immune mechanisms: DC cross-priming (SIINFEKL model antigens in syngeneic system), type I IFN signatures, NK killing of HLA-loss variants, checkpoint ligand modulation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5564225/?utm_source=openai))
- Safety: GVHD grades, cytokine profiles, off-target cytopenias, marrow stromal histology.

Feasibility and innovation
- Feasibility: LSC OXPHOS dependence and metabolic inflexibility create a known vulnerability to acute ROS excursions; the Prx “floodgate” provides a quantitative kinetic target; marrow pO2 is lower than blood, so niche exit inherently increases oxidant pressure; CXCR4/VCAM-1 pathways are established retention axes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8073742/?utm_source=openai))
- Innovation: Converts adhesion force histories into a drug-release logic gate that times a lethal, sub-second oxidant microburst to the precise moment of LSC detachment, creating a system-level selectivity that dose escalation cannot achieve. Shear-unmasking anti-CD47 confines innate/adaptive amplification to mobilized targets, enhancing GVL without exacerbating GVHD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4209443/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Off-target HSC injury: tune force thresholds and pulse amplitude to remain below HSC Prx hyperoxidation rates; schedule carriers when HSCs remain quiescent; verify HSC engraftment capacity post-exposure. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9056110/?utm_source=openai))
- Stromal damage: confirm short diffusion length and rapid decay of oxidants; monitor niche integrity histologically.
- Insufficient mobilization: supplement with brief, low-dose plerixafor; preserve the carrier’s gating to avoid systemic activation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- HLA-loss relapse: leverage NK missing-self and DC cross-priming induced by local anti-CD47; incorporate NK-cell–supportive cytokines post-transplant if needed. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0006497120413564?utm_source=openai))

Success criteria
- Preclinical: ≥1-log reduction of functional LSCs vs RIC alone without impairing donor HSC engraftment; localized immune activation with no increase in GVHD severity.
- Translational path: GMP-ready carrier chemistry; intraosseous or targeted i.v. delivery in early-phase peri-transplant trials to test nonrelapse mortality, relapse incidence, and immune biomarkers.

References (representative)
- LSC OXPHOS dependence and metabolic inflexibility: Lagadinou et al.; reviews. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/9890038/?utm_source=openai))
- Marrow hypoxia and pO2 gradients: Spencer et al.; reviews. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24590072/?utm_source=openai))
- VLA-4/VCAM-1 and CXCR4/CXCL12 niche retention: reviews and clinical mobilization with plerixafor. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6356639/?utm_source=openai))
- Peroxiredoxin hyperoxidation as a rate-sensitive floodgate: Hall et al.; models. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4749870/?utm_source=openai))
- Integrin-tension–gated mechanochemistry: DNA hairpin force probes and force-triggered release. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4209443/?utm_source=openai))
- CD47 blockade enabling cross-priming and antitumor immunity: Liu et al.; reviews. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4598283/?utm_source=openai))
- RIC vs MAC trade-offs: meta-analyses. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7378925/?utm_source=openai))

Expected impact
If validated, rate-thresholded niche-expulsion can replace nonselective genotoxic conditioning by converting a universal, non-molecular discriminator—adhesion force at the niche boundary—into a precisely timed oxidative collapse that only LSCs, not HSCs, cannot buffer. Localized innate/adaptive amplification through shear-unmasked anti-CD47 supplies the missing anti-leukemia potency under RIC/NMA while preserving engraftment and limiting GVHD.

label: debate_bypass
text:
Title
Niche-localized, protease-responsive hydrogel to displace leukemia stem cells and focalize graft-versus-leukemia under antibody-only conditioning

Central hypothesis-question
Can an intraosseous, CXCL12-presenting, protease-responsive hydrogel that physically occupies endosteal/perivascular niches and locally blocks CD47 and PD‑1/PD‑L1 restore myeloablative-level eradication of leukemia stem cells (LSCs) under non-genotoxic antibody conditioning by forcing LSC egress and enabling localized innate/adaptive killing, while preserving donor HSC engraftment and minimizing GVHD?

Rationale (condensed)
- LSCs co-opt marrow niches via CXCR4–CXCL12 guidance and VLA‑4/VCAM‑1 and CD44–hyaluronan adhesion, receiving quiescence and drug tolerance signals; they are protected from systemic therapy and RIC/NMA preserves these sanctuaries. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2723012/?utm_source=openai))
- Post-alloHSCT immune escape frequently involves HLA loss/downmodulation (evading donor T cells, sensitizing to NK), checkpoint upregulation, and CD47-mediated anti-phagocytosis. Systemic PD‑1 blockade can deepen GVL but increases GVHD risk. ([ashpublications.org](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/133/12/1290/260469/Mechanisms-of-immune-escape-after-allogeneic?utm_source=openai))
- Anti-CD47 restores macrophage phagocytosis and can deplete AML/LSCs; local delivery of checkpoint inhibitors via hydrogels or ECM-binding fusion reduces systemic exposure and toxicity while amplifying local immunity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2726837/?utm_source=openai))
- MMP‑2/9 and related proteases are elevated in leukemic marrows and remodel ECM, offering a disease-activated trigger for spatially selective matrix editing and payload release. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12060118/?utm_source=openai))
- Antibody-based, non-genotoxic conditioning (e.g., anti‑CD117/JSP191; CD45‑ADC) can enable allo‑engraftment without busulfan/TBI. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9632731/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Replace systemic “space-making” with niche-local, disease-activated displacement: a marrow-anchored hydrogel creates donor-favoring adhesion/chemokine fields and, upon sensing leukemic proteases, destabilizes LSC adhesion and unmasks them to local innate/adaptive effectors via tethered anti‑CD47 and PD‑1/PD‑L1, thereby recapitulating MAC’s antileukemic functions without systemic genotoxicity.

Specific aims
Aim 1. Engineer an intraosseous, marrow-anchoring immune-adhesive hydrogel (MIAH)
- Features: (i) ECM-anchoring hydrogel (hyaluronic acid/PEG) tuned to marrow stiffness; (ii) immobilized CXCL12 microgradients to bias retention of CXCR4high donor HSCs; (iii) matrix-tethered anti‑CD47 F(ab’) and PD‑1/PD‑L1‑blocking Fabs fused to collagen-binding domains for high local retention and minimal serum spillover; (iv) MMP‑2/9–cleavable linkers controlling on-demand release of microdosed hyaluronan-lyase to weaken CD44–HA–mediated LSC attachment in protease-rich loci. Success criteria: stable depot retention intraosseously; steep peridepot CXCL12 gradient; >10× higher local vs systemic antibody levels; protease-triggered, spatially confined loss of LSC adhesion without impairing donor HSC adhesion in vitro. ([advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://advanced.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/adhm.202304157?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Demonstrate LSC displacement and localized GVL in vivo under antibody-only conditioning
- Model: Primary human AML with LSC content engrafted intrafemorally in NSG; conditioning with anti‑CD117 (JSP191) or CD45‑ADC analog to avoid busulfan/TBI; intraosseous MIAH placement followed by donor CD34+ HSC infusion (IV). Endpoints: (a) displacement kinetics of LSCs from depot-adjacent niches by intravital imaging and CXCL12/CXCR4 trafficking readouts; (b) LSC burden near depot vs distant sites; (c) macrophage phagocytosis of AML (dependence on local CD47 blockade); (d) T/NK activation/exhaustion states near depot (PD‑1 axis). Efficacy readouts: limiting dilution xenotransplantation to quantify functional LSC frequency; MRD by flow and targeted sequencing; donor chimerism and multilineage recovery. Comparator arms: RIC-only; RIC+systemic anti‑PD‑1; RIC+systemic anti‑CD47; RIC+MIAH without antibodies. Target outcome: ≥1‑log reduction in functional LSC frequency vs RIC; equal or better relapse-free survival than MAC historical controls, with reduced systemic toxicity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9632731/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Resolve safety, GVHD, and translatability
- GVHD: Allogeneic mouse models (minor/HLA-mismatch) with MIAH vs systemic checkpoint blockade to quantify GVHD incidence/severity and tissue histology. Hypothesis: ECM-tethered, intraosseous checkpoint/anti‑CD47 yields lower GVHD than systemic dosing at matched local effect. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6310648/?utm_source=openai))
- Off-target: Serum pharmacokinetics of Fabs; biodistribution; marrow cellularity; osteoblast/osteoclast integrity; hematopoietic recovery. Stopping rules tied to anemia (anti‑CD47 RBC interactions), cytopenias, or osteopenia; Fabs are Fc-silent and depot-tethered to limit systemic exposure. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41375-023-01903-2?utm_source=openai))
- Delivery feasibility: Percutaneous intraosseous placement (iliac crest/femur) demonstrated for cells and hydrogels; optimize multi-site dosing to cover ~30–40% of total niche surface without compromising mechanics. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18722042/?utm_source=openai))

Design and methods (concise)
- Hydrogel chemistry: 4‑arm PEG‑maleimide or HA‑tyramine network; incorporate MMP‑cleavable peptides; conjugate CXCL12 via heparin-binding or covalent tethers to create immobilized microgradients; fuse Fabs to von Willebrand A3/lumican collagen-binding tags; validate binding and release in marrow-mimetic bioreactors. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11132073/?utm_source=openai))
- In vitro niche assays: Co-culture human LSC-enriched AML with human MSC/ECM on marrow-stiffness hydrogels; apply MIAH microdepot; measure adhesion forces (traction microscopy), CD44–HA engagement, and protease-triggered detachment; assess phagocytosis by human macrophages ± depot anti‑CD47. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6716085/?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo sequence: Day −7 antibody-conditioning (anti‑CD117 or CD45‑targeted ADC, dose per preclinical guidance); Day −1 intraosseous MIAH; Day 0 donor CD34+ infusion; serial marrow sampling near/far from depot for LSC metrics, single-cell RNA‑seq/ATAC of stromal and immune subsets; systemic exposure of Fabs by LC‑MS. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9632731/?utm_source=openai))
- Statistics/power: Primary endpoint LSC frequency (ELDA analysis); secondary endpoints MRD negativity, relapse-free survival, GVHD grade.

How the proposal meets constraints
- Compensates for reduced-intensity conditioning: mechanical “space-making” and local immune unmasking replace MAC’s stromal injury and systemic cytotoxicity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2723012/?utm_source=openai))
- Excludes non-selective systemic genotoxins: uses anti‑CD117/CD45‑targeted conditioning. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9632731/?utm_source=openai))
- LSC selectivity and sanctuary breach: protease-gated ECM editing weakens LSC-specific adhesion while CXCL12/ECM cues favor donor HSC retention. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12060118/?utm_source=openai))
- Counters multi-axis immune evasion: local anti‑CD47 restores phagocytosis; local PD‑1/PD‑L1 blockade reinvigorates exhausted T/NK in marrow; HLA-loss relapses are vulnerable to NK activity amplified in the checkpoint-relieved microdomain. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2726837/?utm_source=openai))
- Enhances GVL without exacerbating GVHD: depot-tethered, ECM-binding immunomodulators minimize systemic exposure compared with systemic checkpoint therapy associated with GVHD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6310648/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and go/no-go
- Year 1: Optimize MIAH retention, gradient formation, and protease-gated release; in vitro displacement and phagocytosis benchmarks.
- Year 2: NSG xenograft efficacy and PK/PD; pre-specified success: ≥1‑log LSC frequency reduction vs RIC alone and no excess cytopenias.
- Year 3: Allogeneic GVHD models and large-animal intraosseous feasibility; proceed to IND-enabling tox if depot confers superior LSC control with reduced systemic checkpoint exposure.

Exploratory sub-aim (contingent)
- Add ECM-tethered IL‑15/IL‑15Rα microdomain to strengthen NK control of HLA‑loss clones; compare to no‑IL‑15 arms for incremental benefit and safety. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2788234/?utm_source=openai))

Expected outcome
A transplant-adjunct, intraosseous hydrogel that reprograms niche “economics” and focalizes GVL will lower LSC-mediated relapse at least to MAC levels under antibody-only conditioning, while reducing systemic toxicity and GVHD risk through spatially confined immunomodulation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9632731/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Hypoxia-gated, collagen-tethered CD16×CLL1×IL‑15 TriKE factories in the bone marrow to restore RIC/NMA GVL with LSC specificity and minimal GVHD

Rationale
- LSCs exploit BM adhesion and vascular cues (CXCL12/CXCR4, VLA‑4/VCAM‑1, E‑selectin) to enter quiescence, resist therapy, and occupy protected perivascular/endosteal sanctuaries. Disrupting these niche interactions improves leukemia control, but systemic interventions risk harming HSCs. Localizing anti‑leukemia activity to malignant microdomains is preferable. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7290711/?utm_source=openai))
- CLL‑1 (CLEC12A) is expressed on AML blasts/LSCs but absent from normal CD34+CD38− HSCs, enabling LSC‑directed targeting without impairing HSC engraftment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5867061/?utm_source=openai))
- TriKEs (CD16×LSC‑antigen with IL‑15 linker) potently activate NK cells, enhance persistence, and mediate HLA‑independent cytotoxicity; clinical evaluation of 161533 (CD16×CD33×IL‑15) supports platform feasibility. NK alloreactivity provides GVL without driving GVHD. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26847056/?utm_source=openai))
- Hypoxia is a robust feature of AML niches and can be used as a transcriptional address (HRE promoters) in engineered cells. Collagen- or ECM‑binding domains retain biologics in situ, limiting systemic exposure. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8269413/?utm_source=openai))
- CD47 “don’t‑eat‑me” signaling enables LSC immune evasion; bispecifics that block CD47 conditionally on a tumor antigen improve selectivity and mitigate anemia, and protease‑gated “Probody” masking further localizes activity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5368402/?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis–Question (indivisible)
If donor-derived MSCs engineered with hypoxia-inducible control secrete a collagen‑tethered CD16×CLL1×IL‑15 TriKE into leukemic BM microdomains, then early post‑RIC/NMA NK cells will receive spatially focused activation and form high‑affinity bridges to CLL1+ LSCs, overcoming HLA loss and niche protection to reduce relapse without impairing HSC engraftment or inducing GVHD. What level of spatial gating (promoter threshold and matrix‑binding affinity) is necessary and sufficient to achieve LSC clearance with preserved HSC function?

Atomic strategy
Exploit malignant BM physiology as an address code: couple TriKE production to hypoxia and tether the molecule to local ECM, converting protected LSC sanctuaries into NK‑activating kill‑zones while leaving normoxic HSC regions functionally unaltered. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8638314/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
- Aim 1. Build and calibrate the hypoxia‑gated TriKE factory.
  - Construct: MSCs transduced with an HRE-based promoter driving a secreted CD16×CLL1×IL‑15 TriKE fused to a collagen‑binding domain (e.g., LAIR‑2 or lumican CBD) to enforce pericellular/ECM retention. Include a fluorescent reporter via self‑cleaving peptide for real‑time gating readout. Titrate HRE copy number and core promoter to set O2 thresholds (≤1–3% O2). Benchmarks: >50‑fold induction in 1% O2; <5% leak at 5% O2; >80% ECM association within 200 μm of producer cells in BM‑mimetic gels. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8638314/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 2. Demonstrate LSC‑specific, HLA‑independent cytotoxicity and HSC sparing in human BM models.
  - Co‑culture system: primary human donor NK cells + patient‑derived AML (CLL1+ enriched, including HLA‑LOH subsets) + healthy CD34+CD38− HSCs in 3D BM niches under graded hypoxia. Readouts: NK activation (CD107a, IFN‑γ), serial killing, LSC frequency (LDA), HSC CFU‑GEMM/serial LTC‑IC, and bystander toxicity. Controls: non‑tethered TriKE, normoxia, anti‑CLL1 blockade, CD16‑mutant TriKE. Success: ≥10× LSC kill:normal HSC toxicity index; preserved HSC colony output; maintained efficacy against HLA‑deficient AML. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26847056/?utm_source=openai))
- Aim 3. Test efficacy and safety after allo‑HSCT using non‑genotoxic conditioning.
  - Model: NSG or MISTRG PDX with humanized BM; conditioning with anti‑CD117 (briquilimab/JSP191) ± serotherapy to avoid busulfan/TBI; transplant matched donor CD34+ HSCs; intrafemoral delivery of engineered MSCs on day −1 to 0; optional small‑dose donor NK add‑back on day +3 to supply early effectors. Endpoints: leukemia burden, event‑free survival vs RIC alone; donor chimerism; GVHD scores; HSC engraftment; TriKE biodistribution; cytokines. Go/no‑go: ≥50% EFS gain vs RIC control with no GVHD increase and normal trilineage engraftment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12443608/?utm_source=openai))
- Exploratory Aim 4 (contingency for immune evasion): Add a localized, antigen‑conditional CD47 blockade.
  - Engineer MSCs to co‑secrete (under the same HRE control) a CLL1×CD47 bispecific with low‑affinity CD47 arm and high‑affinity CLL1 arm, optionally Probody‑masked for protease activation, fused to a collagen‑binding domain. Test synergy with NK/TriKE by macrophage ADCP assays and in vivo macrophage‑dependent clearance, monitoring hemagglutination/anemia to confirm safety window. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5368402/?utm_source=openai))

Key design choices and justifications
- Target selection for LSC specificity: CLL‑1 is present on AML LSCs and blasts but not on normal HSCs, satisfying engraftment safety. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5867061/?utm_source=openai))
- Effector axis: NK cells operate via missing‑self recognition; TriKE’s CD16 arm supplies high‑avidity, HLA‑independent synapses and the IL‑15 moiety restores proliferation/persistence early post‑HSCT to compensate for RIC/NMA immune deficits with low GVHD liability. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26847056/?utm_source=openai))
- Spatial gating: HRE promoters confine expression to hypoxic leukemic foci; collagen‑binding modules retain the TriKE within BM ECM, minimizing diffusion to normoxic HSC territories and systemic compartments. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8638314/?utm_source=openai))
- Conditioning: anti‑CD117 (JSP191/briquilimab) enables donor HSC engraftment without busulfan/TBI, aligning with the non‑genotoxic constraint. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12443608/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental plan highlights
- Protein engineering: Generate human CD16 (V158‑biased) scFv–IL‑15–CLL1 scFv TriKE with flexible linkers; C‑terminal LAIR‑2 or lumican‑CBD for collagen affinity. Validate binding kinetics (CD16, CLL1; collagen) and IL‑15 signaling. Compare matrix‑tethered vs soluble formats for NK synapse formation and serial killing under shear. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7811803/?utm_source=openai))
- MSC chassis: Human BM‑ or UC‑MSCs transduced with lentiviral vectors encoding HRE‑TriKE‑CBD and a safety switch (iCasp9). Gate calibration by O2 ladder and lactate/pH titration; leak‑proofing with tandem HRE and minimal promoter variants. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12220557/?utm_source=openai))
- BM‑on‑a‑chip: Perivascular/endosteal modules with physiologic O2 gradients; introduce engineered MSCs and track TriKE distribution by fluorescent tags; quantify hypoxia‑dependent occupancy radius and exposure to HSCs vs AML LSCs. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cell-and-developmental-biology/articles/10.3389/fcell.2021.662868/full?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo HSCT: Anti‑CD117‑based RIC/NMA; intrafemoral MSC dosing to seed BM; serial blood/BM pharmacokinetics for TriKE; flow/MRD by CLL1; colony assays for donor HSCs; GVHD histopathology. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12443608/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and mitigations
- Off‑target cytokine stimulation: Matrix tethering and hypoxia gating reduce systemic IL‑15 exposure; monitor serum IL‑15 and CRP/IL‑6; iCasp9 to ablate MSCs if leakage occurs. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7811803/?utm_source=openai))
- Antigen heterogeneity/escape: If CLL1‑low LSCs emerge, switch scFv to alternate LSC antigens or deploy multi‑specific TriKEs in the same gated chassis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5867061/?utm_source=openai))
- Residual macrophage evasion: Deploy conditional CLL1×CD47 bispecific (Aim 4) to add localized ADCP without systemic anemia. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10865928/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and quantitative success criteria
- Year 1: >50‑fold hypoxia induction; ≤5% normoxic leak; ≥80% ECM retention radius ≤250 μm. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8638314/?utm_source=openai))
- Year 2: In 3D BM models, ≥80% reduction of CLL1+ LSCs with ≤10% reduction in HSC CFU; efficacy against HLA‑LOH AML maintained. ([ashpublications.org](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/133/12/1290/260469/Mechanisms-of-immune-escape-after-allogeneic?utm_source=openai))
- Year 3: In allo‑HSCT PDX with anti‑CD117 RIC/NMA, ≥50% improvement in EFS versus control RIC; full donor chimerism; no increase in GVHD; normal trilineage counts by day +100. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12443608/?utm_source=openai))

Readouts that de‑risk translation
- Biodistribution of TriKE (BM vs plasma) and local IL‑15 signaling (pSTAT5 in NK cells) to confirm spatial confinement. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26847056/?utm_source=openai))
- Absence of anemia/hemagglutination; if Aim 4 executed, verify antigen‑conditional CD47 blockade avoids RBC binding. ([aacrjournals.org](https://aacrjournals.org/clincancerres/article/22/20/5109/124860/SIRP-Antibody-Fusion-Proteins-Selectively-Bind-and?utm_source=openai))

Deliverable
A validated, BM‑localized, hypoxia‑gated TriKE‑MSC product that converts leukemic niches into NK‑activating traps, restoring GVL under non‑genotoxic RIC/NMA while preserving HSC engraftment and avoiding GVHD.
