text:
Title
Quorum-gated, locally broadcasting CAR-NK for LSC eradication under non-genotoxic conditioning

Premise and gap
- After reduced-intensity or nonmyeloablative conditioning (RIC/NMA), residual leukemia stem cells (LSCs) persist within CXCL12high, adhesion-rich marrow niches that confer quiescence and immune/drug resistance, and frequently escape via HLA downregulation/LOH, PD-L1 upregulation, and CD47 “don’t-eat-me” signaling. Conventional myeloablative cytoreduction is effective but systemically genotoxic. NK biology offers GVL with low GVHD risk, but current products disperse and are blunted by niche-mediated protection and local checkpoints. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6716085/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic research question (hypothesis and goal merged)
Can donor-derived, bone-marrow–homing CAR-NK cells that activate only when both target engagement and local effector density thresholds are met, and that then broadcast short-range checkpoint/CD47 blockade and niche-disrupting cues, reproduce or exceed MAC-level LSC clearance under non-genotoxic conditioning while preserving normal HSC engraftment and avoiding GVHD?

Core insight (selected element: dual-threshold swarm logic, coupled to local signal broadcasting)
- Population-level quorum gating concentrates NK cytotoxic output where LSCs cluster, preventing wasteful dispersion inherent to RIC/NMA. Once a high-density NK–LSC synapse forms, brief, spatially confined “broadcasts” neutralize PD-1/PD-L1 and CD47 signals and transiently loosen CXCL12/adhesion retention, converting protected niches into kill zones without systemic inflammation. This integrates three biologic truths: LSCs are niche-retained; AML immune evasion is local; NK effectors provide HLA-independent killing with low GVHD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6716085/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation relative to prior art
- Mammalian cell quorum/density control has been engineered but not applied to hematologic graft design; CAR effectors have locally secreted checkpoint inhibitors, and matrix-anchored biologics can confine payloads, yet these have not been combined with NK-based, BM-niche–focused quorum gating to target LSCs after allo‑HSCT. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8995209/?utm_source=openai))

Proposed product concept
- Donor-derived BM-homing CAR-NK (e.g., CLEC12A-CAR for AML LSC recognition) carrying:
  1) A dual-threshold activation circuit: cytotoxicity requires CAR engagement and a rapidly degraded, self-produced quorum cue sensed via a matched receptor, ensuring high local effector density before full degranulation/cytokine output. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8995209/?utm_source=openai))
  2) A contact-triggered local broadcast module: upon licensed killing, NKs release extracellular-matrix–affine mini-bodies that block PD-1/PD-L1 and SIRPα–CD47 within a limited radius, and a brief pulse of CXCR4/adhesion antagonism to dislodge LSCs from niches. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6126939/?utm_source=openai))
- Choice of LSC antigen: CLEC12A (CLL‑1) is frequently present on AML LSCs and largely absent on normal HSCs, preserving donor HSC engraftment. NK missing‑self recognition preserves activity against HLA‑loss variants. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5867061/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims

Aim 1. Establish NK quorum-gated activation that is contingent on target engagement and high local effector density.
- Rationale: Under RIC/NMA, E:T ratios are low; density-gated activation should focus output where LSCs cluster in BM sanctuaries. Benchmarks: ultrasensitive on/off at defined density; suppression of off-target activity in dispersed, antigen-low contexts; preserved function under HLA loss via innate NK receptors. ([escholarship.org](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/0mf694pc?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Engineer and quantify a confined “local broadcast” that neutralizes checkpoints and anti-phagocytic signaling within LSC niches.
- Rationale: Local PD-1/PD-L1 and CD47 blockade enhances cytotoxicity and macrophage phagocytosis but is toxic systemically; ECM-affine fusions restrict spread. Benchmarks: high intraniche vs systemic concentration ratio, enhanced ADCP and NK cytotoxicity, minimal off-niche checkpoint blockade. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6126939/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Demonstrate LSC-debulking and engraftment preservation in RIC/NMA allo-HSCT models without non-selective genotoxic agents.
- Rationale: Must compensate for lost MAC cytoreduction. Benchmarks: reduction of functional LSC frequency, MRD negativity, durable donor chimerism, low GVHD, and preserved donor HSC engraftment. Include CLEC12A targeting to spare HSCs and NK biology to minimize GVHD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5867061/?utm_source=openai))

Study design overview (non-operational)
- Model systems: Human AML LSC–enriched xenografts with humanized BM niches; HLA-loss AML models to test HLA-independent killing; comparative arms with conventional CAR-NK lacking quorum/broadcast modules.
- Readouts: Quorum thresholding (activation vs effector density); spatial pharmacokinetics of broadcasted inhibitors in marrow; LSC frequency by limiting-dilution transplantation; donor chimerism; GVHD indices; niche occupancy and mobilization dynamics upon transient CXCR4/adhesion interference. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11304419/?utm_source=openai))

Mechanistic justifications and expected outcomes
- Niche access and displacement: Transient local antagonism of CXCL12/CXCR4 and adhesion loosens LSC retention and chemoprotection, increasing NK access; prior clinical studies show that CXCR4 antagonism mobilizes AML blasts and sensitizes them to therapy. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22308295/?utm_source=openai))
- Multi-evasion counteraction: NK missing‑self killing covers HLA-loss; local PD-1/PD-L1 and CD47 blockade improves cytotoxicity and macrophage-mediated ADCP without systemic checkpoint toxicity known from systemic agents. ([ashpublications.org](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/133/12/1290/260469/Mechanisms-of-immune-escape-after-allogeneic?utm_source=openai))
- Safety and GVHD: Allogeneic NKs have shown favorable safety and minimal GVHD across trials; ECM affinity curtails systemic exposure to checkpoint/innate modulators. CLEC12A sparing of normal HSCs preserves engraftment. ([mdpi.com](https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/22/9/4590?utm_source=openai))

Risk analysis and contingency
- Risk: Quorum cheating or unintended activation. Mitigation: Incorporate negative feedback on quorum signal production and compare alternative density sensors validated in mammalian circuits. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8995209/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Excess local inflammation. Mitigation: short-lived, matrix-anchored broadcasts with built-in decay; NK platforms historically show low CRS/ICANS. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41423-024-01207-0.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: Antigen heterogeneity. Mitigation: prioritize an LSC-enriched target (CLEC12A); NK innate receptors provide backup against antigen-low clones. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5867061/?utm_source=openai))

Go/no-go criteria
- Clear density-dependent activation with a defined threshold; ≥1-log reduction of functional LSC frequency versus control CAR-NK; maintained donor HSC engraftment with no increase in GVHD signals under non-genotoxic conditioning. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0268960X23000346?utm_source=openai))

Impact
- If successful, this approach replaces indiscriminate MAC injury with a transplant that actively seeks, unshields, and eliminates LSCs while it engrafts, addressing HLA-loss relapse and niche sanctuary—mechanisms central to AML post-transplant failure—without increasing GVHD. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10640763/?utm_source=openai))

text:
Title
Circulation-licensed, engagement-triggered mobilization and killing of AML leukemia stem cells to restore graft-versus-leukemia under non-genotoxic conditioning

Central hypothesis and research goal
Hypothesis: If LSCs are compelled to exit marrow retention and enter normoxic circulation upon target recognition, and if engineered allogeneic effectors are licensed to execute cytotoxicity only in circulation while simultaneously neutralizing checkpoint and anti-phagocytic shields, then relapse after RIC/NMA allo-HSCT can be reduced to MAC-like or lower rates without non-selective genotoxic conditioning. Goal: Develop and test an LSC-selective, compartmentalized immunotherapy that restores early, potent GVL after busulfan/TBI-free conditioning. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1083879111000243?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Invert the niche advantage: use LSC‑antigen recognition to locally convert adhesion/chemokine retention (CXCR4–CXCL12, VLA‑4–VCAM‑1, E‑selectin) into transient dispersal, then gate effector kill by a normoxia-only license so execution occurs in blood, not in hypoxic marrow or parenchyma. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7168055/?utm_source=openai))

Platform overview
- Effector: third‑party allogeneic CAR‑NK cells to minimize GVHD risk and enable off‑the‑shelf deployment; CAR targets an LSC‑preferential antigen (primary: CLEC12A/CLL‑1; alternative: CD123 with HSC-sparing controls). ([ashpublications.org](https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/141/8/856/493324/Allogeneic-natural-killer-cell-therapy?utm_source=openai))
- Recognition‑triggered egress: CAR signal drives local, short‑lived antagonism of CXCR4/VLA‑4/E‑selectin, mobilizing LSCs from BM niche to blood. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Circulation‑licensed cytotoxicity: an oxygen‑sensing OFF‑switch accumulates under hypoxia to suppress NK degranulation; the inhibitor is degraded in normoxia, restoring killing in blood. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- On‑engagement, local immune‑evasion countermeasures: transient, activation‑induced secretion/tethering of PD‑L1 blocking scFv and SIRPα‑Fc decoy to overcome checkpoint upregulation and CD47 “don’t‑eat‑me” signaling at the blood interface. ([jci.org](https://www.jci.org/articles/view/129204?utm_source=openai))
- Conditioning: busulfan/TBI‑free donor‑engraftment using CD117 (c‑Kit) antibody (JSP191)–based regimens ± serotherapy, avoiding non‑selective genotoxic cytoreduction; preserves normal HSC engraftment capacity. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03817-1?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims and methods
Aim 1. Build an LSC-recognition-triggered egress module and quantify mobilization kinetics.
- Design: CAR‑NK specific for CLEC12A (or CD123 in backup cohorts) with an activation-responsive promoter (NK‑validated NF‑κB/NFAT composite) driving: (a) a membrane-tethered CXCR4 antagonist microdomain and (b) secretion of short‑half‑life VLA‑4 and E‑selectin antagonists (peptidomimetics or scFvs), restricted by signal peptides ensuring perisynaptic release. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8595471/?utm_source=openai))
- Models: human AML LSC‑enriched samples in 3D humanized BM‑on‑a‑chip (endosteal+vascular niches; 1%–3% O2 zones) and NSG xenografts. Endpoints: (i) fraction of CLEC12A+CD34+CD38low cells displaced to blood compartment; (ii) time‑to‑peak LSC mobilization (AUC, tmax) with/without each antagonist; (iii) HSC homing/engraftment impact using normal CD34+CD38− cells. Benchmarks: plerixafor and uproleselan positive controls. Safety: reversal of mobilization within 24–48 h after effector removal. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8269413/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2. Engineer and validate circulation‑licensed killing with local checkpoint/CD47 neutralization.
- Design: hypoxia‑OFF cytotoxicity. An intracellular inhibitory binder (“intrabody” or bioPROTAC) targeting a rate‑limiting NK cytotoxic effector (e.g., perforin/ZAP70 homologous signaling node) is fused to the HIF‑1α oxygen‑dependent degradation domain (ODD). Under hypoxia, the inhibitor accumulates and suppresses degranulation; in normoxia, ODD drives proteasomal degradation of the inhibitor, restoring killing. CAR activation simultaneously induces brief secretion or membrane‑tethering of PD‑L1 scFv and SIRPα‑Fc decoy to neutralize adaptive PD‑L1 upregulation and CD47 signaling at the kill site. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- Assays: oxygen‑clamped co‑cultures (1% vs 21% O2) with primary AML (including IFN‑γ–induced PD‑L1high) and HLA‑loss relapse samples; measure degranulation (CD107a), cytotoxicity, and macrophage phagocytosis with/without SIRPα‑Fc. Success criteria: ≥5‑fold cytotoxicity delta (normoxia/hypoxia), ≥2‑fold increase in macrophage phagocytosis with SIRPα‑Fc, and no killing of HSCs under hypoxia. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7412746/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3. Integrate with non‑genotoxic allo‑HSCT and test relapse control against RIC/MAC benchmarks.
- Conditioning: JSP191‑based antibody conditioning (± limited serotherapy) to enable donor engraftment while avoiding busulfan/TBI. Primary readouts: donor myeloid chimerism and CD34+ engraftment kinetics; secondary: infection/GVHD profiles. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03817-1?utm_source=openai))
- Treatment schedule: Day −1 to 0, first CAR‑NK dose to pre‑position in marrow; post‑HSCT Day +3 to +10, repeat short‑lived CAR‑NK pulses to front‑load GVL during aplasia. Rationale: RIC/NMA relies on GVL and has higher relapse risk; early, circulation‑licensed killing compensates for reduced cytoreduction without GVHD escalation typical of broad T‑cell activation. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1083879111000243?utm_source=openai))
- In vivo endpoints (humanized xenograft with co‑infused donor HSCs): (i) MRD negativity in marrow and blood; (ii) leukemia‑free survival; (iii) GVHD scores; (iv) marrow histology for HSC niche preservation. Target: relapse incidence non‑inferior to MAC historical controls with superior non‑relapse toxicity profile. ([astctjournal.org](https://www.astctjournal.org/article/S1083-8791%2818%2930569-X/fulltext?utm_source=openai))

Key design choices grounded in evidence
- Niche retention as targetable vulnerability: AML LSCs exploit CXCR4–CXCL12, VLA‑4–VCAM‑1, and E‑selectin to persist; pharmacologic antagonists mobilize blasts and sensitize to therapy while sparing HSCs when dosed transiently. This validates a mobilize‑then‑treat paradigm to dismantle sanctuary effects. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Checkpoint and anti‑phagocytic shields are rapidly induced/adaptive in AML; local, engagement‑triggered PD‑L1 blockade and SIRPα‑Fc phagocytosis checkpoint disruption have preclinical/early clinical support against AML LSCs. ([jci.org](https://www.jci.org/articles/view/129204?utm_source=openai))
- Hypoxia‑sensing modules are clinically matured but typically “hypoxia‑ON”; inverting by stabilizing an inhibitor under hypoxia exploits the same ODD/VHL axis to create “hypoxia‑OFF” cytotoxicity, confining execution to normoxic blood. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- Allogeneic CAR‑NKs show favorable safety with minimal GVHD/CRS in trials, supporting their use to augment early GVL after RIC/NMA. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-023-02785-8?utm_source=openai))
- LSC antigens: CLEC12A is absent on normal CD34+CD38− HSCs; CD123 is enriched on LSCs but present on subsets of progenitors, justifying CLEC12A as primary target and CD123 as back‑up with tighter safety controls. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5867061/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental details and controls
- Payload localization and half‑life: use signal peptide + transmembrane tethers or scFv–GPI anchors for perisynaptic display; for secreted forms, use PEST/ubiquitin‑fused destabilization to achieve t1/2 <2 h; quantify diffusion radius in microfluidic flow to ensure minimal bystander HSC exposure. Benchmarks: synNotch/TRUCK‑style inducible payload delivery kinetics in T/NK cells. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0092867416312442?utm_source=openai))
- Egress quantification: multiphoton intravital microscopy of calvarial marrow to track labeled LSCs; pharmacodynamic success defined by ≥2× increase in circulating CLEC12A+ LSCs and ≥50% reduction of endosteal LSC dwell time compared with vehicle. Positive controls: plerixafor and uproleselan. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Functional evasion assays: induce PD‑L1 (IFN‑γ) and test HLA‑loss AML relapse samples; measure restored cytotoxicity with local PD‑L1 scFv and enhanced macrophage uptake with SIRPα‑Fc. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7412746/?utm_source=openai))
- Hematopoietic safety: co‑culture with normal CD34+CD38− HSCs under hypoxia; require no excess apoptosis or degranulation signal versus untransduced NK; in xenografts, require preserved donor HSC engraftment and lineage output. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8269413/?utm_source=openai))

Anticipated risks and mitigations
- Antigen heterogeneity/escape: dual‑target CAR (CLEC12A±CD123) with OR‑gate and synNotch‑triggered bispecific NK/T‑engagers to broaden coverage. Go/no‑go: <70% MRD conversion triggers addition of second target. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2022.1085978/full?utm_source=openai))
- Off‑target mobilization (HSC egress): strict activation‑dependence for antagonist release, short half‑life, and dosing windows aligned to donor HSC infusion; abort criterion if >15% reduction in donor HSC marrow lodgment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Hypoxia‑OFF leakage: calibrate ODD‑inhibitor expression to minimize normoxic residual; validate dynamic range using HypoxiCAR benchmarks; add small‑molecule iCasp9 safety switch. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8080111/?utm_source=openai))
- Systemic inflammation: NK platform reduces CRS/ICANS risk; restrict checkpoint/CD47 payload to activation windows and tethered formats to avoid systemic immune disinhibition. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-023-02785-8?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and success criteria
- Year 1: Demonstrate ≥2× LSC mobilization without impairing HSC homing in BM‑on‑a‑chip and NSG; confirm normoxia‑licensed killing with ≥5× normoxia/hypoxia cytotoxicity ratio and checkpoint/CD47 countermeasures restoring kill of PD‑L1high and HLA‑loss AML. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11017789/?utm_source=openai))
- Year 2: Establish busulfan/TBI‑free JSP191‑based engraftment with early post‑HSCT CAR‑NK pulses achieving MRD negativity in ≥70% of xenografts and improved LFS versus RIC‑only controls, with no GVHD signal. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03817-1?utm_source=openai))
- Year 3: IND‑enabling package: biodistribution, shedding, off‑target panel, and GMP feasibility for an off‑the‑shelf CAR‑NK incorporating the hypoxia‑OFF module and activation‑induced, tethered PD‑L1/SIRPα‑Fc payloads.

Why this should meet the clinical bar
- Compensates for RIC/NMA’s reduced cytoreduction by delivering immediate, early GVL in a safe compartment (blood) while stripping niche protection, a combination that historically improved chemosensitivity when done pharmacologically (plerixafor/upro) but not yet coupled to compartment‑restricted cellular cytotoxicity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350358/?utm_source=openai))
- Addresses multi‑axis immune evasion (HLA loss, PD‑L1 upregulation, CD47) at the instant of kill, where local blockade is most efficient and least toxic. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6650729/?utm_source=openai))
- Preserves engraftment by avoiding busulfan/TBI and by suppressing cytotoxicity within hypoxic marrow, protecting normal HSCs. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03817-1?utm_source=openai))

Deliverable
A busulfan/TBI‑free allo‑HSCT adjunct that compels LSCs into a circulation “kill zone,” where allogeneic CAR‑NKs, environmentally licensed and locally disinhibited, deliver precise GVL without GVHD.

Title
pH-gated normalization of adipocyte lactate microdomains to blunt macrophage IL-1β programming in obesity

Premise and rationale
- In hypertrophic adipose tissue, local hypoxia drives a glycolytic shift in adipocytes with increased lactate production and export via monocarboxylate transporters (MCTs), creating lactate/proton-enriched microdomains. This adipocyte-derived signal stabilizes HIF‑1α in neighboring macrophages via PHD2 inhibition, elevating IL‑1β and sustaining depot inflammation. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19876643/?utm_source=openai))
- Human and rodent microdialysis studies demonstrate adipose tissue releases lactate in vivo, with altered regulation in obesity/insulin resistance, supporting a relevant extracellular pool amenable to local interception. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8282793/?utm_source=openai))
- Lactate’s effects on immunity are context dependent; in inflamed obese adipose, lactate augments macrophage IL‑1β via myeloid HIF‑1α, indicating that removing the acidic/lactate enabling condition should decompress inflammatory programming without globally suppressing immunity. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-32871-3?utm_source=openai))
- pH-responsive polymers and histidine/imidazole‑bearing hydrogels can buffer acidic milieus and are established in other tissues, enabling conditional material formation or drug release at mildly acidic pH. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7730929/?utm_source=openai))

Unified hypothesis/question
If we impose pH-gated buffering that forms only within adipocyte-generated acidic microdomains, will normalization of the extracellular lactate/proton condition reduce macrophage HIF‑1α→IL‑1β activation and thereby attenuate adipocyte-driven inflammation without disrupting systemic metabolism?

Atomic strategy
Replace trigger blocking with microenvironment normalization: remove the enabling condition (local extracellular acidosis/lactate accumulation) that allows adipocyte signals to switch macrophages into an IL‑1β‑high state.

Specific aims and experimental plan
Aim 1. Map the coincidence of adipocyte lactate export and extracellular acidosis that predicts macrophage IL‑1β activation.
- Organ-on-a-chip: Co-culture mature adipocytes and primary murine macrophages under normoxia vs hypoxia; quantify extracellular lactate (enzymatic assay) and interstitial pH (ratiometric dyes) across ECM stiffness conditions. Measure macrophage HIF‑1α stabilization and Il1b induction; quantify adipocyte chemokines (Ccl2, Il6). scRNA‑seq of both compartments to resolve lactate/pH‑responsive modules.
- Diet-induced obesity (DIO) mice: Use intradepot microdialysis and pH-sensitive fluorescent probes to validate lactate/pH microdomains; isolate stromal vascular fraction for scRNA‑seq and link macrophage IL‑1β programs to local chemistry.

Aim 2. Engineer a pH-gated buffering microdepot that forms only in acidic adipose interstitium and evaluate its impact on inflammatory programming.
- Material design: An injectable, shear-thinning polymer bearing histidine/imidazole moieties for proton buffering and incorporating acid‑labile crosslinkers (e.g., acetal/imine) to trigger in situ gelation/retention when extracellular pH drops below a preset threshold (target pH 6.6–6.9). Chemistry leverages established pH‑sensitive linkers and histidine-based buffering. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752822/?utm_source=openai))
- Chip validation: Titrate depot formation versus pH; demonstrate minimal gelation at pH ≥7.2 and robust formation at acidic pH. Endpoints: restoration of interstitial pH, reduction of macrophage HIF‑1α and Il1b, decreased adipocyte NF‑κB targets and chemokines, and reduced macrophage chemotaxis.
- Safety/compatibility: Assess adipocyte viability, lipolysis, and insulin signaling; ensure no intracellular acid stress (the buffer acts extracellularly).

Aim 3. Test therapeutic efficacy and specificity in vivo.
- Intra‑depot microinjection in DIO mice: Image depot formation, track interstitial pH normalization, and quantify local lactate. Endpoints: macrophage HIF‑1α target gene expression and IL‑1β protein; adipose cytokines/chemokines; immune cell composition by flow cytometry and scRNA‑seq; systemic glucose and insulin tolerance. Compare to neutral polymer control and systemic alkalinization control (negative comparator for specificity).

Key readouts and analyses
- Chemistry-to-biology linkage: Spatial coupling of pH normalization to suppression of macrophage IL‑1β programs and secondary reductions in adipocyte inflammatory transcripts.
- Single-cell resolution: Loss of lactate/pH‑responsive modules in macrophages and diminution of proinflammatory adipocyte clusters.
- Depot specificity: Minimal effect in lean depots lacking acidification, demonstrating context-dependent activation.

Success criteria
- Demonstration that pH-gated buffering normalizes interstitial pH in obese depots and reduces macrophage HIF‑1α stabilization and IL‑1β without impairing adipocyte viability or whole-body glucose homeostasis. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-32871-3?utm_source=openai))
- Confirmation that effects are contingent on local acidity (no efficacy in neutral pH environments), establishing therapeutic coincidence with the adipocyte-derived enabling condition. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11752822/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and alternatives
- If acidification is insufficiently spatial or persistent to gate the depot, pivot to lactate-absorbing, weak‑base polymers that sequester lactate via reversible ionic pairing while maintaining extracellular pH, or to a dual-trigger design that couples pH‑sensitive crosslinking with lactate‑binding motifs validated in vitro (screened by ITC). Chemistry grounded in the same pH-responsive linker toolbox. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7730929/?utm_source=openai))
- If buffering reduces inflammation but impairs adipose function, titrate buffer capacity and depot density; prioritize partial normalization that preserves adipocyte physiology.

Platforms and feasibility
- Organ-on-a-chip enables controlled creation of hypoxia-driven lactate/pH microdomains and real-time measurement of macrophage responses.
- Transgenic mouse models and DIO paradigms allow intra‑depot delivery and causal testing.
- scRNA‑seq resolves cell-state changes across adipocytes, macrophages, and stromal cells with pathway attribution to lactate/pH signaling. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9445001/?utm_source=openai))

Impact
This work operationalizes adipocyte-derived lactate/proton output as the actionable cause of inflammatory amplification, substituting context-gated microenvironment normalization for pathway blockade. It directly targets the adipocyte mechanism that enables macrophage IL‑1β programming and provides a translationally tractable, locally acting therapy for adipose inflammation in obesity. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19876643/?utm_source=openai))

Title: Rewiring adipocyte lipid-mediator flux with ER–lipid droplet microdomains and EV-directed export to resolve adipose inflammation

Background and significance
- In obesity, adipose tissue develops chronic, low-grade inflammation characterized by adipocyte stress signaling (e.g., NF-κB/JNK), chemokine production (CCL2), and macrophage recruitment that sustains insulin resistance. Obese adipose tissue shows reduced levels of specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) such as RvD1/RvD2, PD1, and MaR1, while exogenous SPMs improve insulin sensitivity and dampen macrophage accumulation in animal models. Subcellular organization determines eicosanoid flux: leukotriene biosynthesis is assembled on perinuclear/ER membranes by 5-LOX and FLAP, and 15-LOX/12-LOX initiate SPM routes from ω-3 PUFAs. EVs from adipocytes carry lipid and RNA cargo that polarize macrophages toward inflammatory phenotypes; conversely, EVs can transport bioactive lipid mediators, including SPMs. Together, these observations indicate that redirecting lipid mediator flux at its subcellular source and using the native EV channel for local delivery could reprogram adipose immune tone. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3424332/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy (single insight)
- Spatially insulate and retarget adipocyte lipid mediator synthesis by building a “resolution microdomain” at ER–lipid droplet (LD) and/or peroxisome interfaces that channels endogenous DHA/EPA into SPMs and preferentially loads them into adipocyte-derived EVs for local delivery to macrophages. This converts a proinflammatory broadcast (adipocyte EVs and eicosanoids) into a pro-resolving one without globally blocking inflammatory pathways. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2919072/?utm_source=openai))

Central hypothesis
- Engineering LOX pathway enzymes to ER–LD contact sites or peroxisomes in adipocytes will increase SPM:eicosanoid ratios at the source and, when coupled to EV sorting, will deliver SPMs to tissue-resident macrophages, restoring efferocytosis and reducing adipose inflammation and insulin resistance. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2919072/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Construct and validate adipocyte “resolution microdomains” that channel ω-3 PUFAs to SPMs.
2) Reprogram adipocyte EVs to export SPM payloads or SPM-enabling mRNAs to local immune cells.
3) Test therapeutic impact on adipose inflammation and systemic metabolism in organ-on-chip and transgenic mouse models, with cell-state resolution by scRNA-seq.

Design and methods

Aim 1: Build ER–LD/peroxisome-targeted SPM microdomains in adipocytes
- Enzyme set and routing:
  - Variant A (PD1/MaR1-biased, avoids 5-LOX): Express human 15-LOX-1 and mouse 12/15-LOX targeted to ER–LD junctions using LD/ER-anchoring motifs (e.g., DGAT2 N-terminus or validated LD-targeting peptides) to produce 17-HDHA and 14-HDHA precursors for PD1 and MaR1. ALOX15 association with LDs supports feasibility of LOX activity at droplet interfaces. ([febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com](https://febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/febs.16266?utm_source=openai))
  - Variant B (RvD-capable): Add a peripherally tethered 5-LOX with FLAP deliberately excluded from perinuclear membranes (mutant 5-LOX lacking strong nuclear localization, with ER–LD anchors) to favor cooperation with 15-LOX products and minimize classical leukotriene assembly at the nuclear envelope. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2629249/?utm_source=openai))
- Compartment targeting:
  - ER–LD contact: use ER hairpin anchors (e.g., DGAT2-like topology) fused to LOX enzymes to confine substrate channeling at nascent droplet necks where LC-PUFA trafficking is concentrated. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11484260/?utm_source=openai))
  - Peroxisome option: append PTS1/PTS2 signals to a low-activity acyl-CoA thioesterase plus LOX to generate local free DHA/EPA and quench H2O2 via catalase, buffering ROS while supporting SPM steps. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6434164/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts (organ-on-chip, primary/mouse adipocytes under flow):
  - Lipid mediator LC–MS/MS: quantify 17-HDHA, 14-HDHA, PD1, MaR1, RvD1/2 and counter mediators (LTB4, PGE2); compute SPM:eicosanoid ratio. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3424332/?utm_source=openai))
  - Adipocyte function: triglyceride content, lipolysis, insulin signaling, adiponectin secretion to confirm preserved core phenotype. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17343838/?utm_source=openai))
  - Microdomain fidelity: proximity ligation and imaging of ER–LD markers (seipin, GPAT4) co-localized with engineered LOX fusions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11484260/?utm_source=openai))

Aim 2: Reprogram adipocyte EVs to deliver pro-resolving signals locally
- EV loading strategies:
  - Lipid mediator loading: enforce enzyme residence within intraluminal budding domains by CD63/CD9 fusions so EV membranes are enriched for SPMs during biogenesis; validate SPM content by LC–MS/MS. EVs physiologically carry eicosanoids/SPMs; engineering amplifies this route. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7313400/?utm_source=openai))
  - Transient mRNA transfer: couple CD9 or CD63 to RNA-binding modules (AGO2/HuR) to enrich stabilized mRNAs for 15-LOX/12-LOX in EVs, allowing recipient macrophages to transiently boost their own SPM production. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9956110/?utm_source=openai))
  - Surface display and targeting: use lactadherin C1C2 fusions to display adhesion/targeting moieties on EVs and enhance payload at the vesicle surface. Optionally adjust integrin composition to favor uptake by adipose-resident macrophages (proof-of-principle informed by exosome integrin tropism studies). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3350974/?utm_source=openai))
- Functional assays (adipose organ-on-chip with resident macrophages):
  - Track EV uptake; measure macrophage efferocytosis, inflammatory cytokines, and SPM receptor activation gene sets (e.g., ALX/FPR2, ChemR23). Demonstrate reversal of adipocyte-EV–driven M1 polarization. ([frontiersin.org](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/endocrinology/articles/10.3389/fendo.2022.839849/full?utm_source=openai))

Aim 3: Test in vivo efficacy with adipocyte-restricted expression and longitudinal single-cell profiling
- Mouse genetics:
  - Knock-in cassette expressing ER–LD–anchored 15-LOX-1±12/15-LOX (±engineered 5-LOX) under adiponectin promoter control; include insulator/UCOE elements to prevent silencing under inflammatory pressure; activate in adipocytes using Adipoq-Cre. Provide dietary ω-3 substrate support in defined cohorts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4281237/?utm_source=openai))
- Endpoints (12–20 weeks high-fat diet):
  - Metabolic: glucose and insulin tolerance; HOMA-IR.
  - Tissue: adipose SPM and eicosanoid profiles; crown-like structure density; flow cytometry of ATM subsets; histology.
  - scRNA-seq/ATAC-seq of SVF and adipocytes: shifts in macrophage states toward pro-resolving signatures; maintained openness and expression at engineered loci across adipocyte subclusters. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9218765/?utm_source=openai))

Key feasibility justifications
- Biology to leverage:
  - SPMs are diminished in obese adipose and their restoration reduces macrophage accrual and improves insulin sensitivity; thus, elevating local SPMs is a validated axis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3424332/?utm_source=openai))
  - Lipid mediator synthesis is spatially regulated; directing LOX enzymes away from nuclear-envelope leukotriene hubs should reduce proinflammatory diversion. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2629249/?utm_source=openai))
  - Adipocyte EVs are established conveyors of inflammatory cues; redirecting their cargo to SPMs is mechanistically aligned and technically achievable. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7916840/?utm_source=openai))
- Tooling to implement:
  - LD/ER targeting and ER–LD contact scaffolds are defined; 15-LOX can function on LDs; peroxisomal targeting via PTS1/2 is routine. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11484260/?utm_source=openai))
  - EV loading via tetraspanin or C1C2 fusions and RNA-binding adaptors (CD9–HuR/AGO2) is documented. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S104620231930266X?utm_source=openai))
  - Adipose organ-on-chip systems that include macrophages exist for human immune–metabolic testing. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9218765/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones and metrics
- M1: ER–LD/peroxisome-targeted constructs increase SPM:eicosanoid ratio ≥3-fold versus cytosolic LOX, with unchanged adipocyte lipid storage and insulin signaling in organ-on-chip. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3424332/?utm_source=openai))
- M2: Engineered adipocyte EVs deliver ≥2× SPM payload versus controls and shift macrophage transcriptional programs toward resolution (↑Arg1/Il10, ↓Tnf/Il1b) under flow. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5979532/?utm_source=openai))
- M3: In mice, adipose SPM levels increased ≥2×, crown-like structures reduced ≥30%, and glucose/insulin tolerance improved versus controls after HFD. scRNA-seq confirms macrophage state reprogramming and stable adipocyte transgene expression. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3424332/?utm_source=openai))

Risk assessment and controls
- Risk: 5-LOX–dependent leukotriene increase. Control by (i) starting with PD1/MaR1-biased Variant A (no 5-LOX), (ii) excluding perinuclear targeting motifs in Variant B, and (iii) benchmarking LTB4/LTC4 levels. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2629249/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: substrate limitation for DHA/EPA in adipose. Mitigation with defined ω-3 supplementation cohorts to ensure adequate precursor pools. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2698663/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: EV off-targeting. Use depot-local administration in mice and size/marker profiling; explore integrin-tuning if needed as an advanced option. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4788391/?utm_source=openai))
- Risk: transgene silencing in inflamed adipocytes. Include UCOE/insulator elements and verify promoter openness longitudinally. ([academic.oup.com](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/43/3/1577/2411815?utm_source=openai))

Deliverables
- A validated genetic toolkit for subcellular routing of SPM biosynthesis in adipocytes and EV-based local delivery.
- Preclinical data in human adipose organ-on-chip and in vivo mouse models demonstrating reduced adipose inflammation and improved metabolic control via source-level mediator reprogramming.

Expected impact
- This strategy directly targets two adipocyte mechanisms that amplify inflammation—eicosanoid flux control and EV signaling—by flipping both toward inflammation resolution with spatial precision, avoiding broad immunosuppression and preserving adipocyte metabolic function. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2919072/?utm_source=openai))

Title: Breaking the mechanical synapse between hypertrophic adipocytes and macrophages to blunt adipose inflammation

Central question/hypothesis:
Does sustained, force-bearing cadherin adhesion between hypertrophic adipocytes and resident macrophages act as a necessary and targetable trigger for adipose inflammation, such that decoupling adhesion from force transmission reduces macrophage inflammatory programming even when adipocytes remain metabolically stressed?

Atomic strategy:
Mechanically uncouple adherens-junction force transmission at adipocyte–macrophage contacts (keep cells viable and in proximity, but prevent α-catenin–vinculin recruitment and downstream YAP/NF-κB activation). This targets a single causal node—the conversion of physical contact into proinflammatory transcription—without broadly suppressing immunity or requiring reversal of adipocyte stress. Force sensing at adherens junctions is mediated by α-catenin conformational switching and vinculin recruitment; these events are sufficient to engage mechanotransduction programs that intersect YAP/TAZ and NF-κB. Direct adipocyte–macrophage contact is known to potentiate inflammatory crosstalk compared with paracrine-only conditions. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms5525?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aim 1. Establish necessity and sufficiency of force-bearing cadherin contact for macrophage inflammatory activation under adipocyte stress (organ-on-chip).
- Platform: Perfused adipocyte–macrophage co-culture chip with (i) controlled contact geometry and duty cycle, (ii) washout of soluble mediators, and (iii) live readouts of junctional load using α-catenin FRET tension sensors and vinculin recruitment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4302114/?utm_source=openai))
- Conditions:
  1) Sustained contact vs nanogap-separated co-culture (a polymer-brush or DNA-spacer interlayer to exceed cadherin trans-dimer reach and prevent cadherin engagement while allowing diffusion).
  2) Pharmacologic decoupling of cadherin mechanotransduction using N-cadherin antagonists (e.g., ADH-1/Exherin; HAV-motif mimetics) to reduce trans binding and load at junctions without killing cells. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8927039/?utm_source=openai))
- Readouts: Single-cell NF-κB nuclear occupancy dynamics, YAP nuclear localization in both cell types, cytokine secretion (TNF, IL-6, CCL2), and scRNA-seq of macrophages for NF-κB/YAP gene modules. Map a “contact-load/time” threshold for stable proinflammatory commitment.
- Predictions:
  - Direct, sustained contact increases NF-κB/YAP activation and inflammatory transcription versus paracrine-only conditions; interrupting cadherin engagement or contact continuity lowers activation despite unchanged adipocyte stress. ([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0085037&utm_source=openai))
  - Junctional mechanosensing signatures (α-catenin opening, vinculin recruitment) correlate with inflammatory outputs and display dose–response to imposed load. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms5525?utm_source=openai))
- Controls and discriminators:
  - Confinement control: spatial confinement alone can dampen some macrophage inflammatory markers; demonstrate that targeted cadherin decoupling reduces inflammatory activation beyond effects attributable to generic confinement. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6615903/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aim 2. Genetically decouple adherens mechanotransduction in adipocytes in vivo and test impact on adipose inflammation.
- Model: Adipoq-Cre–driven expression of an α-catenin mutant in adipocytes that binds cadherin/β-catenin but fails to recruit vinculin under load (mechanically “dead” junction). This preserves tissue cohesion while preventing force-to-signal conversion.
- Intervention: High-fat diet to induce adipocyte hypertrophy and metabolic stress.
- Outcomes:
  - Adipose tissue macrophage states by scRNA-seq (NF-κB and YAP/TAZ target modules), cytokines/chemokines, crown-like structure density, insulin tolerance.
  - Mechanistic biomarkers: reduced α-catenin–vinculin complex formation at adipocyte–macrophage interfaces; decreased YAP nuclear localization in adipocytes. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms5525?utm_source=openai))
- Orthogonal tool: Local delivery of N-cadherin antagonist (ADH-1) to visceral fat to acutely test reversibility of contact-driven inflammation without altering adipocyte size. ([meridian.allenpress.com](https://meridian.allenpress.com/innovationsjournals-JIPO/article/8/1/23/504135/Oncology-Clinical-Trials-Targeting-Members-of-the?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aim 3. Raise the “activation gap” in vivo using a pericellular mechanical shunt to dissipate interface load while maintaining viability.
- Material: Ultra-soft, RGD-modified alginate microgels injected into visceral fat to interpose a compliant, cell-adhesive but force-dissipative layer around hypertrophic adipocytes, thereby reducing cadherin load transfer to macrophages while preserving tissue function. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3389522/?utm_source=openai))
- Rationale: Alginate-RGD is injectable and used in adipose contexts; here, it is repurposed to spread and shunt contact forces away from membranes, lowering α-catenin mechanosignaling and downstream inflammatory transcription. Endpoints as in Aim 2.
- Safety/feasibility: Track macrophage infiltration and polarization after alginate injection; prior work shows biocompatibility in adipose with manageable foreign-body responses. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13112422/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental details and analyses
- Adipocytes: Primary murine adipocytes or human adipocyte cultures exposed to lipogenic stress; macrophages: murine resident-like or human monocyte-derived macrophages.
- Load control: Microactuators in chip to titrate membrane load; quantify α-catenin FRET sensor state and vinculin recruitment in real time. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4302114/?utm_source=openai))
- Transcriptional dynamics: Live-cell NF-κB reporters in macrophages to measure duration-dependent gene regulation; integrate with scRNA-seq to capture stable state transitions. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6465568/?utm_source=openai))
- Mechanistic focus: Distinguish adhesion presence from adhesion load. Show that weakening cadherin trans binding or disabling α-catenin–vinculin coupling reduces inflammatory programming despite continued proximity and metabolic stress.

Expected outcomes and interpretation
- If sustained cadherin load is necessary, then both genetic (α-catenin mutant) and pharmacologic (ADH-1) decoupling reduce macrophage proinflammatory states and improve insulin sensitivity without changing adipocyte size/stress.
- If contact duration thresholds exist, small, periodic separations (nanogap duty-cycling) will prevent stable NF-κB/YAP activation under otherwise identical stress, consistent with duration-tuned inflammatory transcription. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6465568/?utm_source=openai))
- Alternative outcomes:
  - If confinement-dominated effects override junctional signaling (e.g., global dampening of iNOS), then cadherin-specific interventions will not outperform generic spacing. This would falsify the junctional mechanosensing hypothesis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6615903/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation and significance
- Targets a physical→biochemical conversion step (α-catenin mechanosensing at cadherin junctions) rather than downstream cytokines or adipocyte death. This node integrates with YAP/TAZ in adipocytes and YAP/NF-κB crosstalk in macrophages, both active in obesity. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42255-024-01045-4?utm_source=openai))
- Establishes a quantitative “contact-load/time” framework for adipose inflammation, extending prior observations that direct adipocyte–macrophage contact heightens inflammatory outputs. ([journals.plos.org](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0085037&utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Month 6: Chip platform validated; contact vs nanogap delta in NF-κB/YAP with evidence of α-catenin load dependence. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4302114/?utm_source=openai))
- Month 12: “Contact-load/time” activation surface mapped; ADH-1 reduces junctional load and inflammatory transcription without loss of viability. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8927039/?utm_source=openai))
- Month 18: Adipocyte-specific α-catenin mutant cohort profiled; reduced ATM inflammatory states despite persistent hypertrophy and stress markers. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms5525?utm_source=openai))
- Month 24: Alginate microgel shunt demonstrates reduction in macrophage proinflammatory programs in vivo with preserved adipose function. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3389522/?utm_source=openai))

Potential pitfalls and contingency plans
- If N-cadherin is not the dominant cadherin at these contacts, the strategy still holds: the α-catenin–vinculin clutch is the load sensor for classical cadherins; mutants and load-decoupling target this shared mechanotransduction module. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms5525?utm_source=openai))
- If ADH-1 delivery disrupts vascular/endothelial N-cadherin and causes off-target effects, restrict to local, low-dose depot and rely on genetic decoupling to confirm mechanism. ([meridian.allenpress.com](https://meridian.allenpress.com/innovationsjournals-JIPO/article/8/1/23/504135/Oncology-Clinical-Trials-Targeting-Members-of-the?utm_source=openai))

Deliverables
- A validated mechanistic map linking cadherin load at adipocyte–macrophage contacts to NF-κB/YAP activation and inflammatory transcription.
- Proof-of-concept therapeutic modalities: (i) molecular decouplers of cadherin mechanotransduction and (ii) an injectable pericellular mechanical shunt to raise the activation threshold, both reducing adipose inflammation without reversing adipocyte hypertrophy. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8927039/?utm_source=openai))

Title
Adipocyte-intrinsic, inflammation-gated miR-155 sequestration to convert stress signals into autonomous resolution of adipose inflammation

Integrated question–hypothesis
Can adipocytes be reprogrammed so that the very inflammatory activation that elevates miR-155 in obesity instead triggers a local, adipocyte-restricted brake on miR-155, thereby de-amplifying cytokine output and macrophage M1 polarization and resolving adipose inflammation without silencing upstream sensing? In obesity, adipocyte stress (ER stress, lipid overload) activates NF-κB and related pathways and elevates miR-155 in adipocytes and adipose tissue; adipocyte- and macrophage-derived miR-155 reduces SOCS1 and other negative regulators, amplifying inflammatory signaling and promoting M1 polarization. We hypothesize that an inflammation-gated, adipocyte-restricted miR-155 “sponge” will convert stress-induced miR-155 surges into their own neutralization, lowering adipocyte inflammatory transcription and reprogramming adipose immune tone toward resolution. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25647410/?utm_source=openai))

Atomic strategy
Use the inflammatory trigger as therapy: install an adipocyte-restricted, NF-κB–responsive expression cassette encoding a high-capacity competitive decoy for miR-155. When NF-κB activity and miR-155 rise during adipocyte stress, the cassette produces a multivalent miR-155 sponge that sequesters miR-155, derepresses targets such as SOCS1/SHIP1, and reduces adipocyte cytokine/chemokine output that otherwise recruits and polarizes macrophages. This preserves upstream pathogen/stress sensing but breaks the amplification loop at a single, adipocyte-intrinsic node. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6217131/?utm_source=openai))

Specific aims
1) Build and tune an adipocyte-restricted, NF-κB–responsive miR-155 sponge circuit.
- Design: AdipoQ promoter drives a minimal NF-κB response element–containing core promoter linked to a nuclear-stable lncRNA bearing tandem high-affinity miR-155 MREs (10–20 repeats), plus a destabilized GFP reporter for dose calibration. Include a control sponge with scrambled MREs.
- Tuning: Vary NF-κB RE copy number and core promoter strength to achieve low basal expression and strong induction with TNFα/palmitate. Validate adipocyte restriction via AdipoQ specificity. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24480338/?utm_source=openai))

2) Test whether the circuit reduces adipocyte inflammatory output and macrophage M1 polarization under obese-relevant stress in an adipose organ-on-chip.
- Platform: Adipocyte–macrophage organ-on-chip with perfused media; stimuli: TNFα, LPS-primed palmitate, or hypoxia to activate NF-κB/ER stress.
- Readouts: 
  - Adipocytes: NF-κB reporter activity; miR-155 levels; sponge occupancy via AGO2-RIP; SOCS1/SHIP1 protein; cytokines/chemokines (TNF, IL-6, CCL2) in effluent.
  - Macrophages: polarization markers and cytokine profile; sensitivity to adipocyte-conditioned media from sponge+ vs control chips.
- Outcome: Circuit activation should reduce free miR-155, increase SOCS1/SHIP1, and lower cytokine/chemokine output; macrophages exhibit reduced M1 and/or increased M2 markers versus controls. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25647410/?utm_source=openai))

3) Evaluate therapeutic efficacy in vivo using engineered adipocyte transplantation and transgenic models, with single-cell resolution of adipose remodeling.
- Transplantation: Generate sponge+ and control adipocytes ex vivo from stromal vascular fraction, transduce with circuit, and transplant into the subcutaneous or visceral fat of diet-induced obese mice. Compare to sham and to non-induced (NF-κB–silent) controls under low-fat diet.
- Transgenic: Create AdipoQ-Cre–dependent, NF-κB–gated sponge knock-in line for chronic models of obesity.
- Endpoints (12–16 weeks HFD):
  - Tissue: adipose miR-155 levels; SOCS1/SHIP1 protein; cytokine/chemokine panels; crown-like structures; macrophage M1/M2 ratio by flow cytometry and immunostaining.
  - scRNA-seq: infer adipocyte inflammatory states, SOCS1/SHIP1 target derepression, macrophage polarization modules, and intercellular ligand–receptor signaling changes.
  - Systemic: glucose and insulin tolerance; fasting insulin; liver and muscle insulin signaling.
- Success criterion: sponge+ adipose depots show reduced inflammatory transcription, fewer crown-like structures, improved insulin sensitivity, and macrophage repolarization compared with controls. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27671445/?utm_source=openai))

Experimental design details
- Circuit validation
  - Induction dynamics: Time-course after TNFα or palmitate; quantify fold-induction of sponge RNA and decay of free miR-155 by qPCR; confirm reduced loading of miR-155 into AGO2 by RIP.
  - Specificity: Test off-target capture of abundant adipocyte miRNAs by RNA pulldown and small RNA-seq.
  - Thresholding: Introduce a miR-155–sensitive relief-of-repression layer (a short repressor with miR-155 MREs) to sharpen induction only when miR-155 surpasses a pathological threshold; benchmark against linear NF-κB-only control. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6217131/?utm_source=openai))
- Organ-on-chip macrophage assays
  - Use matched BMDMs or human monocyte–derived macrophages; measure polarization after 24–72 h exposure to effluent or co-culture with transwell separation to isolate paracrine effects.
  - Rescue test: Add excess synthetic miR-155 mimic to overwhelm the sponge; reappearance of M1 polarization confirms mechanism.
- In vivo controls
  - Compare to adipocyte-targeted anti-miR-155 antagomir delivery to distinguish circuit advantages (self-dosing, inducibility).
  - Include AdipoQ-Cre–negative littermates to test adipocyte restriction.

Mechanistic and feasibility grounding
- Adipocyte stress in obesity activates NF-κB and elevates adipose miR-155; adipocyte- and ATM-derived miR-155 suppress SOCS1, drive pro-inflammatory signaling, and impair insulin actions. Prior work shows that inhibiting miR-155 enhances adipocyte function and reduces adipose inflammation, yet no adipocyte-restricted, inflammation-gated sequestration strategy has been tested in vivo. The proposed design uses endogenous inflammatory activation as the dosing signal, aiming to reduce amplification while preserving sentinel pathways. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20515657/?utm_source=openai))

Key measurements and analytics
- Molecular: qPCR of miR-155 and sponge; western blot/ELISA of SOCS1/SHIP1 and cytokines; AGO2-RIP for miR-155 occupancy; ChIP–qPCR of NF-κB target promoters.
- Cellular: flow cytometry of adipose SVF for macrophage subsets; multiplex imaging for crown-like structures.
- Single-cell: scRNA-seq to profile adipocytes and immune cells; gene set scoring for NF-κB targets and SOCS1 pathways; cell–cell communication inference.
- Physiology: glucose/insulin tolerance, insulin signaling in adipose/liver/muscle.

Predicted outcomes and discriminating tests
- If the circuit is effective, adipocytes will show lower free miR-155 and restored SOCS1/SHIP1 under stress, reduced cytokine/chemokine release, and macrophages will shift away from M1 polarization; improvements should correlate with sponge occupancy. A direct test is add-back of miR-155 mimic to reverse benefits in chip and in vivo. If benefits occur without reduced free miR-155 or SOCS1 restoration, the hypothesis is falsified.

Potential limitations and mitigation
- Redundancy among inflammatory miRNAs: If other miRNAs compensate, add a second-generation sponge with a limited panel (e.g., miR-146a/b) after verifying their adipocyte upregulation in the same contexts.
- Over-suppression risk: AdipoQ restriction and NF-κB gating minimize effects in lean states; expression kinetics and degradation tags will be tuned to avoid chronic suppression.
- Species differences: Validate in human adipocyte–macrophage chips and human adipose explants to de-risk translation. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9249816/?utm_source=openai))

Why this meets the goal
- Direct target: adipocyte-intrinsic inflammatory amplification via miR-155.
- Flip of trigger: the same NF-κB/miR-155 surge that normally drives inflammation now triggers its own neutralization.
- Platforms: organ-on-chip for mechanism and paracrine testing; engineered adipocyte transplantation and transgenic mouse for in vivo efficacy; scRNA-seq for state-resolved readouts.

Optional comparative aim (mechanistic orthogonality; not required for primary hypothesis)
- Install an adipocyte-restricted, stress-gated DGAT1+PLIN1 module to increase FA re-esterification and LD shielding only during inflammatory activation; benchmark effects on ER stress markers and macrophage polarization against the miR-155 sponge. Prior work shows DGAT1 activity protects adipocytes from lipotoxic ER stress and inflammation, supporting this comparator. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6195226/?utm_source=openai))

Milestones
- Months 0–6: Circuit construction, induction tuning, and mechanistic validation in adipocytes on-chip.
- Months 6–12: Paracrine macrophage assays and rescue experiments on-chip; finalize in vivo dosing/transplant protocols.
- Months 12–24: In vivo efficacy and scRNA-seq analyses; optional comparator testing and human adipose validation.

Title
Preventing the adipocyte inflammatory switch by temporally biasing lactate partitioning and GPR81 signaling, guided by spatial 13C flux imaging

Rationale
- In hypertrophic adipocytes, glycolytic overflow elevates lactate, shifts redox, and increases extracellular lactate that engages the Gi-coupled receptor GPR81 (HCAR1), which is highly expressed in differentiated adipocytes and mediates potent anti-lipolytic signaling. Thus, lactate is both a metabolic byproduct and a signaling input that can modify the stress trajectory of adipocytes. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19047060/?utm_source=openai))
- ER stress sensor IRE1α links metabolic/secretory burden to inflammatory outputs (JNK, NF-κB), and its activity rises in adipose tissue during obesity; its kinase arm specifically couples inflammatory cues to adipocyte-autonomous lipolysis. Early modulation can bias outcomes before full inflammatory commitment. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6901316/?utm_source=openai))
- Histone lysine lactylation is a lactate-derived epigenetic mark with distinct temporal dynamics from acetylation; it is present in adipose tissue and can modulate gene expression programs. Preventing an early surge of intracellular lactate could reduce lactylation-driven transcriptional priming. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1678-1?utm_source=openai))
- Spatially resolved stable-isotope tracing by MALDI-MSI enables in situ mapping of 13C label propagation through metabolites at near single-cell resolution in tissues, providing a practical trigger to detect pre-switch glycolytic/oxidative inflections in specific adipocytes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10926149/?utm_source=openai))

Central hypothesis-question
Can transiently biasing lactate partitioning—lowering intracellular lactate/lactylation while preserving or enhancing extracellular GPR81 activation precisely at pre-inflammatory glycolytic spikes—prevent the adipocyte fate switch into an inflammatory state?

Atomic strategy
Exploit lactate’s dual identity. At predicted pre-switch windows, decouple intracellular lactate (chromatin/redox driver) from extracellular GPR81 signaling (anti-lipolytic/anti-inflammatory) using timed metabolic and receptor interventions guided by spatial 13C flux imaging.

Specific aims

Aim 1. Define the pre-inflammatory “switch window” in adipocytes by spatial 13C flux imaging and single-cell state mapping.
- Platforms: adipocyte–endothelium organ-on-a-chip with controllable glucose, O2, and fatty acid gradients; high-fat-diet (HFD) mice.
- Tracers and imaging: pulse [U-13C]glucose and [U-13C16]palmitate; acquire high-resolution MALDI-MSI of adipose slices/chips to quantify isotopologues of lactate (M+3), pyruvate (M+3), citrate (M+2), acylcarnitines (M+2), and UDP-Glc labeling; co-register with histology and spatial transcriptomics anchors. Compute a per-cell “switch index” (glycolytic flux up, β-oxidation down, citrate export up). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10926149/?utm_source=openai))
- Single-cell readouts: scRNA-seq to quantify early inflammatory priming (e.g., Ccl2, Il6), stress reporters, and adipocyte identity genes.

Milestone: Quantify time/location of flux excursions that precede inflammatory transcription by 6–24 h.

Aim 2. Test whether timed GPR81 activation combined with intracellular lactate minimization blocks the switch.
- Interventions (chip):
  - GPR81 axis: short pulses (30–120 min) of a selective GPR81 agonist delivered only at switch-index peaks to suppress cAMP/PKA and acute lipolysis, lowering ER load. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19047060/?utm_source=openai))
  - Lactate partitioning: CRISPRi/a to bias LDH isoforms (↓LDHA, ↑LDHB) and modulate MCT1/4 to favor pyruvate recycling and controlled export, thereby reducing intracellular lactate (and H3K18la) while allowing sufficient extracellular lactate to drive GPR81. Small-molecule LDH-A inhibitors will be used as orthogonal tools.
- Readouts:
  - CUT&Tag for H3K18la and H3K18ac at inflammatory enhancers; NF-κB/JNK activity reporters; cytokines.
  - scRNA-seq with Perturb-seq barcodes to link gene perturbations to transcriptional states.
  - 13C-MSI pre/post-intervention to confirm flux correction.
- Decision rule: If timed GPR81 agonism alone is insufficient, combine with LDH/MCT biasing; if excessive lactate export elevates paracrine effects, titrate MCT modulation to maintain local but not systemic lactate increases.

Aim 3. Validate prevention in vivo with adipocyte-specific genetics and timed dosing.
- Mouse lines: Adipoq-CreERT2;LDHAfl/fl (or CRISPRi), Adipoq-CreERT2;MCT1fl/fl, and Gpr81+/+ vs Gpr81−/− controls.
- Protocol: Initiate HFD; at week 2–3 (early hypertrophy), perform tracer gavage for switch-index mapping; deliver short-acting GPR81 agonist doses at empirically determined windows; in genetic arms, induce LDHA knockdown to lower intracellular lactate.
- Endpoints: adipocyte inflammatory fraction by scRNA-seq; adipose cytokines; crown-like structures; systemic lipolysis indices; depot-specific 13C flux correction.

Experimental design and analyses
- Organ-on-chip experiments will use microfluidic O2 and substrate gradients to reproduce hypoxia/substrate overflow and allow repeated, time-locked interventions.
- Spatial 13C MSI data will be normalized to serum tracer enrichment and integrated with cell-type annotations to resolve per-adipocyte flux. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10926149/?utm_source=openai))
- Statistics: mixed-effects models for spatially nested measurements; preregistered primary outcome is reduction in inflammatory adipocyte fraction at sites/times with elevated switch index.

Predicted outcomes
- Timed GPR81 activation will acutely dampen lipolysis and lower ER/inflammatory signaling during glycolytic spikes; LDH/MCT biasing will reduce H3K18la and transcriptional priming; together they will prevent the emergence of inflammatory adipocyte states without chronically suppressing baseline lipolysis or adipocyte function. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19047060/?utm_source=openai))

Falsification and contingency
- If prevention fails despite confirmed GPR81 signaling and reduced H3K18la, then lactate partitioning is not the gating variable; pivot to IRE1α timing as an alternative early node using transient IRE1 RNase/kinase inhibitors at switch-index onset to decouple JNK/NF-κB outputs (tested on-chip, then in adipocyte-specific IRE1α alleles). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021925821002131?utm_source=openai))
- If 13C-MSI cannot resolve single-adipocyte flux in WAT due to lipid content, implement validated sample-prep enhancements for adipose to improve metabolite detection and maintain spatial integrity. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9114030/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- Reframes lactate from a chronic byproduct to a time-gated, dual-mode control signal and exploits its partitioning to prevent, not treat, the adipocyte inflammatory switch.
- Uses spatial 13C flux imaging as a trigger to schedule brief, local interventions, enabling causality tests in heterogeneous adipose tissue.

Impact
- Provides a prevention-first, mechanism-anchored strategy to reduce adipocyte-driven inflammation by resolving when to intervene and which facet of lactate biology to engage—extracellular receptor signaling versus intracellular chromatin/redox—thereby minimizing systemic side effects while preserving adipocyte function.

text:
Title
Stress-gated braking of adipocyte lipolysis to convert inflamed white adipose tissue into a healing, weight-neutral organ

Premise and Rationale
- Obesity shifts adipocytes into a mechanically and metabolically stressed state that activates mechanotransduction (YAP/TAZ, Piezo1, FAK) and inflammatory transcriptional programs. Adipocyte mechanosensing is heightened with hypertrophy and matrix stiffening, and YAP/TAZ activation correlates with adipose inflammation and fibrosis. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9367348/?utm_source=openai))
- Nutrient excess elevates ROS and lipid peroxidation, which license NLRP3 inflammasome activity in adipose tissues; adipocyte GPX4 restrains lipid peroxidation and protects against adipose inflammation and systemic insulin resistance. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7312293/?utm_source=openai))
- Adipocyte lipolysis via ATGL (PNPLA2) is a dominant source of FFA flux that shapes adipocyte-intrinsic lipotoxic signaling and paracrine crosstalk with macrophages. Pharmacologic ATGL inhibition (Atglistatin) lowers adipose macrophage infiltration and inflammatory markers in vivo; however, complete genetic ATGL ablation can provoke BAT inflammasome activation, indicating benefit from partial, context-limited inhibition. Moreover, FFA released from adipocytes may be insufficient alone to activate macrophages, underscoring the value of controlling intracellular lipotoxic stress in adipocytes. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7847076/?utm_source=openai))

Hypothesis–Question (inseparable)
Can a threshold-gated, adipocyte-intrinsic brake on ATGL-dependent lipolysis—activated only when lipid peroxidation risk rises—raise the inflammatory activation threshold of adipocytes, reduce macrophage recruitment, and convert obese white adipose tissue into an inflammation-resolving state without requiring weight loss?

Atomic Strategy
Couple an oxidative-stress sensor to a reversible, partial repression of PNPLA2 in adipocytes. When lipid peroxidation increases, the sensor transiently lowers ATGL activity, reducing intracellular and paracrine lipotoxic signals that prime NF-κB/NLRP3; as stress resolves, ATGL returns to baseline to preserve systemic metabolic flexibility. This directly targets adipocyte drivers of inflammation (ROS/peroxides, lipolysis-derived signals) while avoiding constitutive pathway blockade. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7312293/?utm_source=openai))

Specific Aims
Aim 1. Map the stress thresholds that trigger adipocyte inflammatory transition and quantify how partial ATGL inhibition and enhanced peroxide detoxification shift these thresholds.
- Platform: human adipocyte–macrophage adipose-on-chip with tunable ECM stiffness and perfused lipotoxic stress (palmitate ± high glucose). Readouts: YAP nuclear localization, Ca2+ transients (Piezo1 activity), NF-κB reporter, ROS (HyPer), lipid peroxidation (BODIPY-C11), NLRP3 activation (ASC specks/caspase-1), adipokines, and macrophage polarization. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9367348/?utm_source=openai))
- Interventions: graded Atglistatin (0–10 µM) to model partial ATGL inhibition; doxycycline-inducible GPX4 in adipocytes to elevate peroxidation thresholds. Outcomes: dose–response surfaces for inflammatory readouts; scRNA-seq to identify MHO-like adipocyte states and ATM phenotypes at constant lipid load and stiffness. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7847076/?utm_source=openai))
- Decision criterion: identify a parameter window where ATGL inhibition reduces inflammatory outputs without impairing adipocyte viability or β-adrenergic responsiveness.

Aim 2. Engineer and validate a stress-gated ATGL “brake” circuit in adipocytes.
- Construct: AREmin–rtTA→TetO–dCas9-KRAB targeting PNPLA2 (gRNAs validated on-chip), leveraging endogenous NRF2 activation by oxidative stress (ARE). In parallel, TetO–GPX4 provides rapid peroxidation quenching to prevent ferroptotic/DAMP signaling. Circuit logic: oxidative stress ON → transient PNPLA2 repression + GPX4 upshift; stress OFF → release repression. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41366-022-01064-9?utm_source=openai))
- Validation on-chip: closed-loop dynamics (time to engage/disengage), magnitude of PNPLA2 knockdown (target 30–60%), maintenance of acute lipolytic capacity upon β3-agonist challenge after stress resolution, and macrophage responses to conditioned media. Safety guard: cap KRAB dwell time with Tet-off washout to prevent over-suppression noted in ATGL genetic ablation contexts. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6439276/?utm_source=openai))
- Success metric: circuit reduces NF-κB/NLRP3 activation and macrophage proinflammatory markers under stress, with preserved lipolytic competence post-stress.

Aim 3. Test therapeutic efficacy and weight-neutrality in vivo using transgenic mouse models.
- Models: (i) Adipoq-rtTA; TetO-dCas9-KRAB::PNPLA2 gRNA (stress-gated via AREmin–rtTA knock-in at Rosa26) and (ii) Adipoq-rtTA; TetO-GPX4. Diet-induced obese mice receive doxycycline to enable circuits; a separate arm receives oral Atglistatin for benchmarking. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7847076/?utm_source=openai))
- Endpoints at fixed body weight: adipose tissue crown-like structure density, adipocyte YAP target gene expression, ROS/lipid peroxidation indices, NLRP3 activation, ATM composition and states by scRNA-seq, adipokine profile, glucose/insulin tolerance. Mechanistic control: evaluate BAT to ensure no inflammasome activation (guarding against over-suppression); titrate doxycycline to partial PNPLA2 repression. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9367348/?utm_source=openai))
- Primary success criterion: reduction in adipose inflammatory signatures and ATM recruitment with unchanged body weight and preserved acute fasting lipolysis.

Experimental Design and Analyses
- Organ-on-chip: matrix stiffness sweep (0.5–15 kPa) × palmitate (0–500 µM) ± Atglistatin/GPX4. Mixed-effects models quantify main and interaction effects on inflammatory readouts; determine the minimal PNPLA2 repression that maximally reduces inflammatory outputs.
- scRNA-seq: integrate adipocyte and immune compartments; define transcriptional programs resembling metabolically healthy obesity; infer ligand–receptor signaling changes.
- Mouse studies: power for 20–25% reduction in CLS density and IL-1β with α=0.05, β=0.8. Include pair-fed controls to fix weight. Pharmacodynamic biomarkers: adipose glycerol/NEFA release ex vivo ± isoproterenol to confirm partial lipolysis preservation.

Anticipated Outcomes and Interpretation
- Partial, stress-contingent suppression of ATGL will dampen adipocyte-intrinsic NF-κB/NLRP3 activation and reduce macrophage recruitment at constant adiposity, shifting adipose tissue toward a healing, resolution-biased state. GPX4 co-induction increases the peroxidation threshold that licenses inflammasome activity, complementing the lipolysis brake. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7847076/?utm_source=openai))
- Weight neutrality is expected because basal lipolysis and β-adrenergic responsiveness are preserved when stress is absent; failure to preserve these would indicate oversuppression, consistent with pathology observed in complete ATGL deficiency. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6439276/?utm_source=openai))

Potential Risks and Mitigations
- Over-inhibition of ATGL: limit PNPLA2 repression to <60%, incorporate time-capped KRAB activity, and verify BAT safety. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6439276/?utm_source=openai))
- NRF2/ARE off-target effects: use minimal ARE promoter and adipocyte-specific rtTA; validate specificity by scRNA-seq and off-target transcriptional profiling. ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41366-022-01064-9?utm_source=openai))
- FFA–macrophage activation ambiguity: prioritize adipocyte-intrinsic stress readouts and macrophage responses to whole adipocyte-conditioned media rather than isolated FFAs. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26245186/?utm_source=openai))

Innovation
- Reframes adipocytes as adaptive homeostats: a closed-loop, threshold-gated brake on lipolysis that operates only under danger conditions, directly targeting adipocyte mechanisms that increase inflammation (peroxidation-licensed NLRP3 activation and lipolysis-driven stress), and achieves therapeutic reprogramming without weight loss. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7312293/?utm_source=openai))

Go/No-Go Milestones
- Go: organ-on-chip demonstrates ≥30% reduction in NF-κB/NLRP3 readouts with ≤20% loss of β-adrenergic lipolysis post-stress; mouse arm shows ≥25% reduction in CLS at matched weight. No-Go: evidence of BAT inflammasome activation or persistent lipolysis impairment despite titration. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6439276/?utm_source=openai))
